directions.name: Instrument
directions.oneLiner: A quiet graphite instrument panel: monochrome hairline grid, mono readouts, and exactly one signal-colored control lit on each screen, which is always the thing to press next.
directions.vibe: The app works like a well-made device you pick up every morning. The surfaces are paper-grey and graphite, the numbers sit in exact columns, the labels are small engineered caps, and nothing moves unless something changed. Because the chrome is silent, every puzzle reads clearly. The single lit accent (the next game's Play key, then your Share key) turns the daily ritual into a short sequence you can read at a glance. The warmth comes from the people, through names, ranks and the rank-change ticks, and not from decoration. That is what keeps it premium instead of noisy after 300 days of use.
inspirations: Teenage Engineering OP-1 / EP-133: signal orange on grey, numbered mono labels, one lit key
Braun ET66 calculator (Dieter Rams): monochrome body with one colored key for the primary action
Linear: Inter, hairline dividers, fast exact transitions, dense but calm lists
Things 3: list rows as the primary object, generous row height, quiet completion states
Josef Muller-Brockmann grid systems: 4px baseline, ruled section headers, flush-left type
SBB / Swiss railway departure boards: tabular countdowns and readouts you trust
Vignelli NYC subway signage: the rollover is New York midnight, so the type is functional and signage-like

typography.notes: Three roles, kept strict. (1) Inter Tight 600, only for names and titles: page/greeting H1 28/32px at -0.025em, play-header game name 17/22px at -0.015em, section H2 20/24px at -0.02em. Word-game tiles also use it, at 700, uppercase, 24px. (2) Inter for everything you read: body 15/22px at 400, row titles 16/20px at 600, secondary text 13/18px in muted. Inputs are always 16px so iOS Safari does not zoom. Set font-feature-settings 'cv05','cv08' globally so lowercase l has a tail and capital I has serifs. That matters for word puzzles, where I and l must never be confused. (3) JetBrains Mono 500 for every number and label: scores, ranks, points, countdown, puzzle number (N°142) and the tiny-caps labels. The tiny-caps label style is JetBrains Mono 500 at 11/16px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.06em, color muted. It is never smaller than 11px and never used for primary information. Readout values are 20/24px mono with tabular-nums. The result score is mono 64/64px at -0.04em, with '/100' at 20px in muted. Ranks are zero-padded ('01', '02'), and ties show as '=3'. Load only what is used: Inter variable (latin), Inter Tight weight 600 only, JetBrains Mono weight 500 only, all through next/font/google with display: swap. That is roughly 100KB woff2 in total. If the bundle budget is tight, drop Inter Tight and use Inter 600 with -0.025em tracking at display sizes; the look survives.

shape.texture: A dot grid on --bg only: background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 1px 1px, var(--grid-dot) 1px, transparent 0); background-size: 24px 24px; with --grid-dot set to rgba(17,17,18,0.07) in light and rgba(237,237,234,0.05) in dark. It aligns to the 4px layout grid (24 = 6 units). It is switched off on the play route (play layout sets background-image: none), so the puzzle never sits on a pattern. Cards, the game stage and inputs are solid surface. The spoiler wall uses a second, functional pattern: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, transparent 0 5px, var(--border) 5px 6px).
shape.notes: The radius scale is near-square: 4px for chips, badges and in-game tiles/cells; 6px for buttons, inputs, avatars and the emoji tile; 8px for cards, the game stage and the segmented-control track. There are no pills and no fully rounded shapes except the 6px status dot. Borders are 1px hairlines in --border for structure (dividers, card edges), which are decorative and allowed to be low contrast. Add a --border-strong token for anything interactive that is identified by its outline (inputs, outlined chips, unselected tabs): #858580 in light (3.71:1 on surface, 3.10:1 on surface-2) and #6A6A6E in dark (3.39:1 on surface, 3.09:1 on surface-2), which meets WCAG 1.4.11. Focus rings are 2px solid var(--fg) with 2px offset, monochrome so they pass on every surface. Elevation is mostly absent: the hierarchy comes from hairlines and the bg vs surface step, not shadows. The only real shadow is the segmented-control thumb: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.08) in light, none in dark. Spacing is a 4px baseline with the steps 4/8/12/16/24/32/48, a 16px page gutter, and a max content width of 480px.

directions.motion: Motion is fast, exact and never decorative. Tokens: --dur-1 90ms (press and hover color shifts), --dur-2 160ms (chip/toggle state, segmented thumb slide, crossfades), --dur-3 240ms (panel enter, spoiler reveal, list reorder), --dur-4 420ms (score digit roll, points-bar growth). --ease-out is cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1) for anything entering or settling; --ease-in is cubic-bezier(0.4,0,1,1) for exits, which run at 0.75x their enter duration; linear is used only for the countdown and progress hairlines. There are no springs, overshoot or bounce, and nothing scales on press: the current active:scale-[0.98] is removed. Filled buttons get active:translate-y-px plus filter: brightness(0.94); rows and outlined controls shift to bg-surface-2 over 90ms. Only transform, opacity and clip-path are animated, for mid-range Android performance, and there are no blur or backdrop-filter animations. Route changes are instant with no page transitions. Staggers are capped at 6 items x 24ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion, every duration becomes 0 except opacity fades at 120ms, and numbers render at their final value.
directions.soundAndHaptics: Both are off by default, since people play in bed, on trains and next to others. Each has its own toggle in Profile (SOUND / HAPTICS). Sound is synthesized with WebAudio, with no audio files and the AudioContext created lazily on the first user gesture. Key press is a 2ms square-wave tick at 3kHz, gain 0.04. Submit is a 6ms tick at 1.8kHz. Solve is two sine notes, 880Hz then 1320Hz, 70ms each with 10ms between. Fail is one 220Hz sine at 120ms. Rank-up is three ascending ticks of 40ms each. Haptics use navigator.vibrate, which is Android Chrome only. iOS Safari has no vibration API, so the toggle is hidden there rather than showing a dead control. Patterns: key 6ms, submit 10ms, solve [12,60,12], fail [30]. Games never call audio or vibrate directly. They emit platform events (feedback('key'|'submit'|'solve'|'fail')), so every future game sounds and feels the same and respects the user's toggles.

signatureMoments.design: When the last move resolves, the game stage stays put and the result card enters underneath: opacity 0 to 1 and translateY 8px to 0 over 240ms ease-out, then the page scrolls it into view. The score is a mechanical counter. Each digit is a vertical strip of 0-9 inside a 1em overflow-hidden window, translated with translateY(-n*1em) over 420ms ease-out, staggered 60ms from the rightmost digit leftwards, like an odometer. The '/100' suffix and the 'SOLVED · 4/7' label (tiny caps) are static, so only the number moves. The share grid then builds row by row, 24ms apart, each row fading in over 120ms. The solve sound and haptic fire on the last digit settling, if enabled. Reduced motion shows the final number immediately.

The share grid sits in a surface-2 box with 6px radius, emoji at 20px with 24px line-height and 2px letter-spacing, above a mono line showing the exact header text that will be sent ('Number Hunt N°142 · 87/100'), so what you see is exactly what gets sent. At this point Share is the screen's one accent-filled button, 52px tall and full width, with #0B0B0C ink. It calls navigator.share and falls back to the clipboard. On the clipboard path the label crossfades to 'Copied' with a check glyph over 160ms, and a 1px accent hairline under the button drains from 100% to 0% width over 1600ms linear, then the label reverts. There is no toast.

The Today hub's stat strip has a NEXT readout counting down in mono (04:12:33), with a full-width 2px day-progress hairline under the strip. The hairline is filled in accent to the fraction of the New York day that has elapsed, so you can see how much of today is left. At 00:00:00 New York time the hairline completes and resets to 0 over 240ms, and the date line and the 'N°142' puzzle number roll to the next value with the same digit-strip mechanism. Game rows crossfade their status to PLAY with a 24ms stagger, and a one-line tiny-caps banner, 'NEW PUZZLES · N°143', sits under the header for 4s and then fades. There is no confetti and no modal. A tab left open overnight wakes to the new day without a reload.

Leaderboard rows are FLIP-animated when points change, moving only translateY over 240ms ease-out, with your row on top in z-order. Your row's points bar grows from its old width to its new width over 420ms. A delta tag appears beside the rank: mono 11px '▲2' in --good or '▼1' in --bad, measured against the standings the last time you viewed this board (stored per period). It persists until the next rollover, so friends who check later still see the climb. When you move up, the rank-up tick sound plays if enabled. The row's 2px accent left rule is always present, which marks 'you' without needing color text.

Before you finish, the friends' results panel is a card filled with the 135deg hatch pattern (1px --border lines on a 6px pitch). Centered on it is a solid surface plate with 'LOCKED · FINISH TO SEE 4 RESULTS' in tiny caps. It is still useful while locked: each friend who has finished is listed by avatar, name and finish time, and their score cell is a fixed 48x20px hatched block, so revealing causes no layout shift and leaks nothing. When your result lands, the hatch layer is removed with clip-path: inset(0 0 0 100%) animating from inset(0) over 240ms ease-out, wiping left to right like a shutter. The scores then run the digit roll with a 40ms row stagger.

The STREAK readout on the Today hub is the number in mono plus a 7-cell strip of 8x8px squares with 4px radius and 2px gaps, like a sequencer row. Days played are filled with --fg, missed days are outlined in --border-strong, and today is outlined in accent until you play one game, then it fills. There is no flame emoji in the UI; the flame lives only in the share text.

directions.gameCardTreatment: The Today hub lists games as rows inside one card (8px radius, 1px border), separated by hairline dividers, Things-style, instead of a stack of separate cards. Each row is a full-width link, at least 76px tall, with 16px padding, laid out as a CSS grid with columns 20px, 40px, 1fr and auto, and 12px gaps. Column 1 is the index number in tiny-caps mono ('01'), top-aligned. Column 2 is a 40x40 emoji tile (6px radius, bg-surface-2, emoji at 22px, with no accent tint). Column 3 has three lines. The first is an 8x8px square swatch in the game's accent, then the name in Inter 600 16px. The second is the tagline in Inter 13px muted, truncated. The third is a tiny-caps meta line in mono: '5/8 FINISHED', or 'NO ONE YET'. Column 4 shows the status. NEXT-UP, which is the first unfinished live game in display order, is the screen's only accent fill: a 32px-tall chip with 4px radius and 12px horizontal padding, mono 12px 600 uppercase 'PLAY' in #0B0B0C on the game's accent, plus a 2px accent inset rule on the row's left edge (box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--accent)). Other unplayed rows get the same chip outlined (1px --border-strong, fg text). In-progress rows get an outlined 'CONTINUE' chip, plus a segmented progress meter under the meta line. The game reports a fraction, rendered as N cells of 6x2px, filled in fg up to that fraction. Done rows have no chip. Instead they show the score in mono 22px tabular with '/100' in muted at 13px and the game's native label (4/7) in tiny caps beneath. The row keeps full contrast; finishing is a fact, not a dimming. Testing games get a 'TEST' badge: mono 10px, 1px dashed --border-strong, 4px radius. The stat strip above the list is three equal cells divided by vertical hairlines (DONE 1/3, STREAK 12 plus the tick strip, NEXT 04:12:33), with labels in tiny caps over 20px mono values. The greeting drops the wave emoji: 'Good evening, Ashwin.' in Inter Tight 28px, with '05 OCT 2026 · MON' on the left and 'N°142' flush right in tiny caps above it.
directions.leaderboardTreatment: Game tabs are a horizontally scrolling row of 36px-high chips with 4px radius, extended to a 44px hit area with an ::after pseudo-element: OVERALL first, then each game with its 8px swatch and name. The selected tab is fg fill with bg text, which is monochrome, so the accent stays reserved. Unselected tabs are transparent with a 1px --border-strong outline. On a per-game tab, the page's --accent is set to that game's color. Below the tabs, the period control is a full-width 3-segment control (TODAY / WEEK / ALL TIME, in tiny-caps mono): a 40px-high track (44px hit area) in bg-surface-2 with 8px radius and 3px padding. The selected thumb is bg-surface with a hairline border and a small shadow, and slides over 160ms. The table is one card. A header row in tiny caps reads '# PLAYER STK PTS', and every row uses the same grid-template-columns of 28px, 28px, 1fr, 40px and 52px with 10px gaps, so columns align exactly from row to row. Rows are 56px tall (48px in the compact 5-row 'STANDINGS' block on Today). Rank is mono 13px zero-padded ('01'): fg for the top 3 and muted after. The avatar is a monochrome 28px square with 6px radius, bg-surface-2, a 1px border and Inter Tight 600 12px initials. The viewer's avatar is inverted (fg fill, bg text). Under the name in Inter 500 15px is a mono 11px muted second line: '4 GP · AVG 78' on overall, or the native label on per-game tabs ('4/7'). Streak is plain mono (12). Points are mono 600 16px, right-aligned, tabular. Each row has a 2px points bar along its bottom edge, from the name column to the right edge, with width equal to points divided by the leader's points: --border-strong at 50% opacity for others, accent for your row, which is the only accent in the table besides your 2px inset left rule on a bg-surface-2 row. Players who haven't played sink below a tiny-caps 'NOT PLAYED' divider, with rank '—' and the whole row in muted. Delta tags (▲2 / ▼1) sit beside the rank, as described in Rank change.
directions.playScreenFrame: The platform owns everything around the game, and the game owns only the Stage. (1) The header bar is 52px and sticky, on bg with no blur. On the left is a 44x44 back button (chevron icon, ghost). In the center are the emoji at 18px and the game name in Inter Tight 600 17px. On the right is 'N°142' in tiny caps. Directly under it, a full-bleed 2px rule in the game's accent: the one signal that you are inside this game. The dot-grid texture is off on this route. (2) Before starting, a pre-start card shows the rules as a numbered list: mono tiny-caps '01', '02' in a 24px column, Inter 15/22 text. Under the rules is a tiny-caps meta line ('≈2 MIN · 7 GUESSES · SCORED 0-100'), then a full-width 52px accent 'Start' button with #0B0B0C ink and 6px radius. That button is the screen's only accent fill. (3) A readout strip sits between the header and the stage. Games declare HUD values as data, for example readouts: [{label:'GUESS', value:'3/7'}, {label:'RANGE', value:'12–48'}], and the platform renders them as tiny-caps labels over 20px mono values in equal cells divided by hairlines. Every game's HUD therefore looks the same, and games never style their own status text. (4) The Stage is a surface card with 8px radius, a 1px border and 16px padding, with a reserved min-height so it does not jump. It has no texture, no shadow and no ambient motion. Inside it, games get CSS variables (--stage-gap: 8px, --cell: computed square size from the available width) and a fixed state vocabulary they must use instead of raw colors. HIT is a --fg fill with --bg glyph. NEAR is an --accent fill with #0B0B0C glyph. MISS is --surface-2 with a --muted glyph. EMPTY is a 1px dashed --border-strong outline. Errors are --bad text and confirmations are --good text. HIT, NEAR and MISS differ by luminance, not hue (hit vs miss is 15.8:1 in light and 14.2:1 in dark; near vs miss is at least 3.09:1), so they read correctly with color-vision deficiency. Platform primitives (Tile, Cell, Key, Keyboard, Meter, ChoiceList, Readout) carry these styles, at 4px radius, a 44px minimum key height and 16px input text. (5) Validation messages appear in one fixed slot under the stage, 13px, in --bad. Platform notices use a single-line surface-2 bar above the readouts. Nothing overlays the stage while you play. (6) After finishing, the result card, Share, and then the friends panel (or the spoiler wall) stack below the stage. The accent fill moves from Start to Share.
directions.scalesToNewGames: A new game supplies data, never styling: id, name, emoji, one accent hex, a tagline, rules, readouts, and a UI component built from platform primitives. Accent rule: every game accent must have WCAG relative luminance between 0.20 and 0.24. The six provided accents all fall in that band. That band mathematically guarantees four things: #0B0B0C ink on the accent is at least 4.9:1; the accent is at least 3.35:1 against light bg and surface; it is at least 3.09:1 against light surface-2; and it is at least 4.18:1 against every dark surface. So one hex works in both themes with no dark variant. The rule is enforced in src/games/registry.test.ts with a 6-line luminance check, so an out-of-band color fails CI. The current Number Hunt amber #f59e0b (luminance about 0.46, 2.1:1 on white) would fail and must move to one of the six, for example cobalt #2F7BF5. The accent is never text; it only fills chips and tiles and draws rules, swatches and bars. The HIT/NEAR/MISS/EMPTY vocabulary covers every planned genre. Word games: tiles. Logic grids: cell fills and given/derived marks. Number games: meter segments and readouts. Map games: region fills (HIT fg at 85% so borders stay visible, NEAR accent). Chart games: the series in --fg at 1.5px, the highlighted or guessed series in accent at 2px, other series in --muted at 1px, gridlines in --border, axis labels in tiny-caps mono. Social/quote games: options in a ChoiceList where selected is a fg fill, the correct answer reveals with a --good check glyph, and quotes are set in Inter 18/26. A lint rule (no-restricted-syntax or a simple grep in CI) bans raw Tailwind palette classes (text-sky-*, bg-emerald-*, and so on) and text-accent inside src/games. Game identity comes from the emoji tile, the 8px swatch, the header rule and the Play/Start/Share fills, so twenty games never turn the hub into a rainbow: at most one row is lit at a time.
risks: It can read as cold or corporate, a 'Linear clone', for a friends' game. Warmth has to come from copy (first names, 'Good evening, Ashwin.'), the people-centric leaderboard and the share moment. If the group finds it sterile, the cheapest warm-up is shifting bg toward #F5F3EF, not adding color.

Monochrome square avatars remove at-a-glance color identity for friends. Names always sit next to avatars, which mitigates it, but with more than 8 players recognition slows. A fallback is a 2px hue-derived underline on the avatar only.

The 0.20-0.24 luminance band rules out bright yellows, limes and pastels as game accents; yellow at that luminance is olive. A future game whose identity is 'yellow' must use ochre or rely on its emoji.
HIT as a solid fg tile (black in light, white in dark) breaks Wordle's green-tile muscle memory. Players may need one round to adjust, and the rules panel should show a 3-tile legend.

11px mono tiny caps are at the edge of comfortable reading on small phones for older eyes. They must stay secondary, never drop below 11px, and keep muted at 5.6:1 or better (it currently reaches 5.62 on light surface-2 and 6.04 on dark surface-2).
The 24px dot grid can moire or shimmer on some low-DPI Android screens when scrolling. Drop it, which is a one-line change, if it shows up on real devices.
Three font families (about 100KB) add first-load cost on mid-range phones over cellular. Collapsing Inter Tight into Inter is the mitigation.
The 'accent is never text' and 'one accent fill per screen' rules are easy to erode as features are added. They need a lint check and a review habit, or the calm degrades.
Haptics only work on Android, because iOS Safari has no vibration API, so the experience differs across the group.
directions.buildNotes: 1) src/app/globals.css. Replace the token values with the light and dark sets above, using the same accent #EC4F17 in both themes. Add tokens: --border-strong (#858580 light, #6A6A6E dark), --accent-ink: #0B0B0C, --grid-dot (rgba(17,17,18,0.07) light, rgba(237,237,234,0.05) dark), --dur-1: 90ms, --dur-2: 160ms, --dur-3: 240ms, --dur-4: 420ms, --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1), --ease-in: cubic-bezier(0.4,0,1,1). In @theme inline, add --color-border-strong, --color-accent-ink, --font-sans: var(--font-inter), --font-display: var(--font-inter-tight), --font-mono: var(--font-jetbrains-mono), --radius-sm: 4px, --radius-md: 6px, --radius-lg: 8px, --shadow-card: var(--card-shadow), with --card-shadow defined per theme. Add utilities: @utility label { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-size: 11px; line-height: 16px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: .06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--muted) } and @utility num { font-family: var(--font-mono); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums }. On body, set font-feature-settings: 'cv05','cv08' and the dot-grid background. Add a .hatch class with the 135deg repeating-linear-gradient. Add a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block that zeroes the duration tokens. 2) src/app/layout.tsx. Swap Geist and Geist_Mono for Inter, Inter_Tight({weight:'600'}) and JetBrains_Mono({weight:'500'}) from next/font/google, using variables --font-inter, --font-inter-tight and --font-jetbrains-mono. Change the themeColor values to #F4F4F2 and #0B0B0C. 3) src/components/ui.tsx. BUTTON_BASE becomes 'inline-flex h-12 items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md px-5 text-[15px] font-semibold transition-[background-color,filter,transform] duration-[var(--dur-1)] active:translate-y-px disabled:opacity-40'. The accent variant becomes 'bg-accent text-accent-ink active:brightness-95' (replacing text-black). The secondary variant becomes 'border border-border-strong bg-surface'. Card becomes 'rounded-lg border border-border bg-surface shadow-card'. SectionTitle renders a 'label' on the left, an optional right meta or link in 'label', and a 1px border-b with pb-2 mb-3. Field gets a label-style caption, an input with 'h-12 rounded-md border-border-strong text-base', and focus via 'outline-2 outline-offset-2 outline-fg'. Avatar becomes a 'rounded-md bg-surface-2 border border-border font-display' initials square with an 'inverted' prop for the viewer, and the hsl pastel is deleted. New primitives: Readout({label,value}), StatStrip, Segmented (radiogroup plus a sliding thumb using transform), Chip (filled, outlined or selected), ScoreRoll (digit strips), Hatch, TickStrip, and a feedback() hook for sound and haptics. 4) src/components/game-card.tsx becomes a GameRow inside a single list Card. The page passes isNextUp, which is true for the first unfinished live game. Implement the swatch, index, meta line, chip states and done-score layout described above, and drop the left w-1 accent bar and the accent/15 emoji tint. 5) src/components/leaderboard-table.tsx. Each li gets grid-cols-[28px_28px_1fr_40px_52px] gap-2.5, plus a header row, a points bar (absolute bottom-0 h-0.5 with width as a percentage of the leader's points), the viewer style 'bg-surface-2 shadow-[inset_2px_0_0_var(--accent)]', a NOT PLAYED divider, delta tags, and FLIP reorder (a small hook using getBoundingClientRect and the Web Animations API, with no library). 6) src/app/(app)/page.tsx. Replace the greeting block with a date/N° tiny-caps line, a 'Good evening, Name.' H1 in font-display, a StatStrip (DONE, STREAK with TickStrip, NEXT with Countdown in num) and a day-progress hairline. 7) src/app/(app)/play/[gameId]/game-host.tsx. Add the sticky header with the 2px accent rule, the numbered rules list, a readouts slot (extend GameUiProps or the game definition with readouts(view)), the Stage wrapper, a result card with ScoreRoll, a WYSIWYG share preview box, and the spoiler-wall component with the clip-path reveal. 8) src/games/number-hunt. Change the accent in logic.ts to an in-band hex (for example #2F7BF5). In ui.tsx, replace the sky/rose/emerald classes with tokens: 'Higher ↑' and 'Lower ↓' in fg with a mono arrow glyph, 'Got it' in text-good, errors in text-bad, text-black becomes text-accent-ink, rounded-xl becomes rounded-md, and the guess rows use the EMPTY dashed --border-strong style. 9) src/games/registry.test.ts. Assert that every game accent's relative luminance is between 0.20 and 0.24. 10) src/components/bottom-nav.tsx and brand-mark.tsx (not reviewed, adapt accordingly). The bottom nav uses tiny-caps labels with a 2px fg top rule on the active tab rather than an accent color. The brand mark becomes a 12px accent square next to the wordmark in Inter Tight 600. Verified contrast: fg/bg is 17.14 (light) and 16.77 (dark). Muted is 6.71 on light surface and 6.62 on dark surface, and stays at least 5.62 on surface-2 in both themes. Good and bad on surface are 5.43 and 5.66 (light) and 9.07 and 7.15 (dark). #0B0B0C on the six accents is between 4.94 and 5.34.

directions.name: Toy Box
directions.oneLiner: Everything you can tap is a chunky candy key with an ink outline that clicks down 4px when pressed. Finished games stay pushed in, so you can see what's left at a glance.
directions.vibe: It feels like a desk toy you fidget with every morning. The base is warm cream paper with confident ink outlines, and color only shows up on keys, game stickers and tiles. Ink outlines and hard shadows make the app feel handmade and a bit cheeky, which fits a private friends' club rather than a polished consumer brand. The depth rules always mean the same thing. A lip under something means you can press it. A diagonal offset means it is a static sticker. Flat means it is a calm work surface. So it stays playful without turning noisy, and the puzzle tray in the middle stays quiet.
inspirations: Duolingo: 3D lipped buttons, and a dark mode where the lip is lighter than the background so it reads as the side of a block
Gumroad (2021+ rebrand): 2px ink outlines, hard offset shadows, candy fills with black text
Balatro: each colored button has a darker lip in its own color on a dark table, and chunky score count-ups
NYT Connections: flat candy tiles with dark text as the model for in-game state tiles
FigJam stickers: slightly tilted cut-out stickers with hard shadows
Teenage Engineering hardware: keys that travel when pressed, and a monospace readout for numbers

typography.notes: Load with next/font/google as Bricolage_Grotesque (variable, latin subset; variable: --font-display), Figtree (variable 500-800; variable: --font-sans; the only one preloaded) and Space_Mono (weight ['400','700']; variable: --font-num). Space Mono is monospaced, so scores, countdowns and points line up without relying on a tnum feature. Type scale: the hub H1 is Bricolage 800 at 32/36 with -0.03em tracking. Game titles are Bricolage 700 at 22/26 with -0.02em. Section labels are Figtree 800 at 12px, uppercase, 0.1em tracking, in muted. Body text is Figtree 500 at 16/24, and meta lines are Figtree 500 at 13/18 in muted. Button labels are Figtree 800 at 16px, sentence case and never all caps (to keep it calm). Numbers: the result score is Space Mono 700 at 64/64 with a muted '/100' at 20px. Leaderboard points are Space Mono 700 at 18px. The countdown and the puzzle number ('#142') are Space Mono 700 at 13-14px. The share receipt is Space Mono 400 at 13/20. Emoji fall back to the system emoji font. Never set Bricolage below 18px, because its quirky shapes muddy at small sizes. Expected font payload is about 130KB woff2 in total. Only Figtree is preloaded, and the other two use display: swap.

shape.texture: A dot grid on the body only: background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 1px 1px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 9%, transparent) 1px, transparent 0); background-size: 22px 22px; background-attachment: scroll (fixed causes repaint jank on iOS). It never appears inside cards, the game tray or tiles. The spoiler wall is the only other texture: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, transparent 0 8px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 6%, transparent) 8px 16px) on surface2.
shape.notes: Radius scale: keys and inputs 12px, stickers/cards 16px, the game tray 20px, chips and avatars fully round. Every outline is 2px, never 1px or 3px. In light mode the outline is ink #1E1830 (16.8:1 on surface). In dark mode it is lilac slate #7E72A6 (3.8:1 on surface, 4.29:1 on bg, which passes the 3:1 non-text rule for input boundaries). There are three depth levels, each with one fixed meaning. (1) KEY, for anything interactive: a straight-down lip, box-shadow 0 4px 0 0 var(--key-edge). Light mode uses ink for --key-edge. Dark mode uses color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 50%, #000) on accent keys (e.g. tangerine gives #80451F, 2.47:1 on bg) and #7E72A6 on neutral keys. Pressing it translates the key down 4px and the lip collapses to 0. (2) STICKER, for static info such as standings, result and stats: a diagonal 4px 4px hard shadow, using ink in light and #4A3F66 in dark. That dark color is lighter than bg (1.94:1), so it reads as the block's side face, Duolingo-style; a black shadow would vanish at 1.09:1. The result card gets a 6px 6px 'prize' sticker shadow. (3) FLAT, for the game tray, leaderboard rows and tiles: no shadow. All shadows have 0 blur, so they are cheap to paint. Dividers inside stickers use --hairline (light: color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 14%, var(--surface)); dark: #3A3150), not ink, so dense lists don't look like a spreadsheet.

directions.motion: Motion is driven by physical presses and only ever animates transform and opacity. The one exception is the 4px lip box-shadow on small keys. Key press: the base rule has transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1), box-shadow 180ms (same curve), and the :active rule overrides it with transition-duration 70ms; transition-timing-function cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1). The key snaps down fast and springs back with about 2px of overshoot. Result sticker 'stamp' (240ms, spring curve): scale 1.06 and rotate -1.5deg go to 1 and 0deg, and the shadow grows from 0 to 6px 6px. The score counts up from 0 over 600ms with ease-out-cubic, using requestAnimationFrame on the Space Mono digits. Share-grid tiles pop from scale .7 to 1 over 140ms with a 35ms stagger, and the total stagger is capped at 600ms. Leaderboard reorders use FLIP over 320ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). At midnight, done cards pop back up over 220ms on the spring curve with a 60ms stagger. The spoiler wall peels off with translateX(101%) over 320ms, cubic-bezier(.7,0,.3,1). Route changes have no slide transitions: navigation is instant, plus an optional 120ms View Transitions cross-fade where the browser supports it. Inside the game tray the platform animates nothing; games may use the shared key press on their own keys. With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, every transform transition is set to 0.01ms, the count-up shows the final number, staggers are removed, and only 120ms opacity fades remain. Nothing loops or idles on screen. The one exception is the countdown ticking once per second, and only its text changes.
directions.soundAndHaptics: Sound is OFF by default, with a toggle on Profile (stored per device in localStorage). When on, every sound is synthesized with WebAudio, so there are no asset downloads. The key click is a 4ms white-noise burst through a 2.2kHz bandpass with a 40ms exponential decay at about -24dBFS, played on pointerup and not pointerdown, so scrolling never clicks. Solving plays two sine notes, C6 then G6, 80ms each with 10ms attack. A loss plays a single soft triangle wave at A4 for 120ms. A share copy plays a single 1.5kHz 'tick'. Nothing plays on page load or rollover. Haptics use navigator.vibrate where it exists (Android Chrome): 8ms on key release, [12,40,18] on solve, 20ms on share copy, and nothing on errors or losses, so it never feels like a buzzer. iOS Safari has no vibrate API. We accept that for now. The input type=checkbox switch label trick could fake haptics there later, but it is a hack and is not part of the baseline. A game cannot trigger sound or haptics directly. It calls the platform's feedback('tap' | 'solve' | 'fail'), so the volume and settings stay in one place.

signatureMoments.design: After the last move, the game tray stays put and a prize sticker stamps in below it (6px 6px shadow, 240ms spring). Its top band is the game's accent fill with ink text ('Solved · 4/7' or 'Not this time · 7/7', Figtree 800 at 14px), 2px ink rule below. The body shows the score in Space Mono 700 at 64px, counting up over 600ms, with a muted '/100' after it. Underneath is the share grid as tiles popping in with a 35ms stagger, then a full-width accent Share key (56px tall). A 'Not this time' result uses the same layout with the band in surface2, not red: losing should never feel punished.

Above the Share key, a 'receipt' box shows the exact text that will be pasted: surface2 fill, 2px dashed border, Space Mono 400 at 13/20. Pressing the key calls navigator.share. If that's unavailable, the clipboard fallback runs and the key changes for 1.8s to a mint (#3FD68F) fill with an ink '✓ Copied' label, haptic 20ms and the tick sound when enabled, then reverts. The key stays the same size, so the layout doesn't shift.

The countdown is a 'ticket' chip: 2px ink outline, Space Mono 700 'NEXT 06:14:22', with semicircle notches cut into both sides using radial-gradient masks. In the final hour its fill turns lemon. If the PWA is open across midnight in New York, a sticker banner drops in at the top, 'Fresh puzzles are in', with a Refresh key. After refreshing, every pushed-in Done card pops back up into a raised key (220ms spring, 60ms stagger), so you see the board 'reset'.

The last-seen rank per board and period is stored in localStorage. If the viewer's rank changed, their row FLIP-animates from the old position to the new one over 320ms. A climb shows a mint chip with ink '▲2' (Space Mono 700, 12px). A drop shows a surface2 chip with a muted '▼1', never red. Reaching #1 gives the rank medallion a one-time 'stamp' animation (scale 1.15 to 1, rotate -6deg to 0).

Below your unfinished game, friends' results sit in a locked card: surface2 fill, 2px dashed border, the -45deg hatch texture, and a 🔒 tile. The title reads 'Finish to peek' (Bricolage 700 at 18px), followed by a 20px avatar stack, 'Maya, Dev +2 finished', and their scores as '??' chips in Space Mono. The per-game Today leaderboard uses the same '??' hatched chips. When you finish, the hatch layer slides off to the right over 320ms and the friend rows pop in with a 40ms stagger, each showing an avatar, name, their share grid and their score.

When you finish a game, its Today card stays permanently pushed in: translateY(4px), no lip, surface2 fill, the ink outline kept, a '✓ 87' score chip in Space Mono with a mint fill, and a 'See results' label at full fg contrast, so it doesn't look disabled. Raised cards are what's left to play. Pushed-in cards are done.

The streak chip shows 🔥 plus the count in Space Mono 700. At 7, 30 and 100 days it switches to a lemon fill with ink text and a 4px 4px sticker shadow, and plays one 'stamp' animation the first time it is shown.

directions.gameCardTreatment: Each Today card is a full-width KEY, at least 76px tall, with a 16px radius, surface fill, 2px outline and a 4px lip. It sets data-accent and the --accent style, so the derived tokens resolve for that game. Left: a 52px emoji tile with the game's accent fill, a 2px ink outline and a 12px radius. The tile is tilted -4deg while the game is unplayed and straightens to 0deg once started, so it reads as a sticker peeling into place. Middle: the name in Bricolage 700 at 18px. Below it, the tagline in Figtree 500 at 14px in muted (truncated). Below that, a social line: a stack of 20px avatars (overlapping by -6px, each with a 2px surface ring) plus '3 finished' in 13px muted. Right: a status pill, 32px tall, fully round, 2px outline. 'Play →' is an accent fill with ink text. 'Continue' is --accent-tint (22% accent over surface; fg contrast 14:1 or better) with a three-dot progress indicator. 'Done' cards follow the pushed-in rule from the signature moments (a mint '✓ 87' chip and no lip). A 'Testing' badge for admins is a dashed-outline chip with an uppercase 10px muted label. Above the list sits a 'day meter': one 2px-outlined pill slot per live game, filled with that game's accent when finished, next to '2 of 3' in Space Mono. It replaces the current '0 of N done today' sentence.
directions.leaderboardTreatment: Game tabs are a horizontal scroller of 40px chips. Each has a 2px outline, an emoji and the name in Figtree 700 at 14px. The selected chip is pushed in (translateY(2px), no lip) and filled with that game's accent, or lemon for Overall. Unselected chips are surface with a 2px lip. Give the scroller 6px of bottom and right padding so lips and shadows aren't clipped. The period control is a 44px track with a surface fill, 2px outline and 12px radius, split into Today / Week / All-time. The selected segment is inverted: an ink fill with bg-colored text (15.6:1 in light). In dark mode it is an fg fill with bg text (16.7:1). Rows live inside one STICKER, separated by --hairline dividers, at least 60px tall with 16px horizontal padding. Left: a 28px rank medallion with a 2px ink outline and the rank in Space Mono 700 at 13px. Gold is #FFD43B, silver #D9D4E6 and bronze #F2A66E, all with ink text at 8.5:1 or better. Ranks 4 and below are plain Space Mono with no fill, and players who haven't played show '–' in muted. Next comes a 36px avatar (pastel hsl(h 75% 78%) with an ink initial, 6.9:1 or better, and a 2px ink ring). Then the name in Figtree 700 at 16px, with a meta line '5 played · avg 72 · 🔥 9' in 13px muted. On per-game Today boards, the native label (e.g. '4/7') sits in a surface2 chip in Space Mono. Right: points in Space Mono 700 at 18px, right-aligned, 56px column. The viewer's row gets a highlighter background, color-mix(in srgb, #FFD43B 32%, var(--surface)) in light (#FFF0BB; fg 15:1, muted 6.2:1) and 16% in dark (#453931; fg 10:1, muted 5.1:1), plus a small ink 'YOU' chip. Rank-change chips work as described in the signature moments. The Today hub's mini standings reuse the same component limited to 5 rows, inside a sticker, with a small 'Full board →' ghost link.
directions.playScreenFrame: The platform puts every game in a fixed frame of four parts. (1) A header row: a 44×44 back key (surface fill, ← glyph, 3px lip); the game label (32px accent emoji tile plus the name in Bricolage 700 at 20px); and on the right a puzzle-number chip ('#142 · Mon 5 Oct', Space Mono 700 at 12px, 2px outline). (2) Before starting, a rules sticker: an accent top band reading 'How to play' in ink, then the rules as a numbered list with 24px ink-outlined Space Mono number circles, then a 56px full-width accent 'Start ▸' key. (3) The GAME TRAY, which is the calm zone: surface fill, 2px border, 20px radius, NO shadow, no texture, 16px padding, full content width. The tray sets CSS variables that game UIs consume: --tile-size: clamp(44px, 12vw, 60px), --tile-radius: 10px, --tile-border: 2px, plus the state tokens --hit #3FD68F, --near #FFD43B, --miss var(--surface2). All three take ink text at 9:1 or better. Tray rules for game authors: use only tokens, no Tailwind palette colors; text is only fg or muted, never accent; tiles are FLAT; only the game's own input keys and submit button may use the KEY lip; accent covers at most about 20% of the tray area; no tilt or decorative motion. Tiles may use a 90ms press scale of .96 when typed into. For colorblind safety, state never relies on color alone: --near tiles also get the hatch pattern and --hit tiles get a 3px inset ink ring via box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--ink) on top of the 2px border. On-screen keyboards for word games use mini-keys: at least 52px tall, as wide as space allows (about 32px on a 375px screen), with a 3px lip. Server notices show as an ink-outlined toast pinned above the bottom nav, with a 4px left stripe in --bad. (4) Below the tray: the result sticker, then either the friends' results or the spoiler wall. The page sets data-accent and --accent on its root so every derived token re-resolves for that game.
directions.scalesToNewGames: A new game provides exactly one accent hex and one emoji. Everything else is derived from tokens. Derived tokens are declared on ':root, [data-accent]', so they re-resolve wherever --accent is overridden: --accent-tint = color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 22%, var(--surface)) (18% in dark), and --accent-lip = var(--ink) in light or color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 50%, #000) in dark. Ink (#1E1830) is the only text color ever placed on an accent, so any accent with at least 7:1 against ink works in both themes. The six candy swatches measure 7.29-12.18:1. As fills they rely on the 2px outline for their boundary in light mode (fill-to-surface contrast is only 1.4-2.7:1, which is why the outline is mandatory) and stand out at 6-11.7:1 on dark surfaces. Add a check to src/games/registry.test.ts that computes WCAG contrast of every game.accent against #1E1830 and fails below 7:1, so Ashwin can pick any hex and CI catches a bad one. Game UIs build from four exported primitives in ui.tsx: Key, Tile, Tray, Sticker. They also use the shared state tokens --hit, --near and --miss, which match the share-grid emoji 🟩🟨⬜, so word and logic-grid games feel like a family. Map and chart games: strokes are fg at 2px, regions are surface2, the selected region is accent with an ink outline, and categorical series use the six candy swatches, each with a 2px ink outline, so they stay distinct in both themes. Number and quote games: text in Figtree or Space Mono on the tray; accent only for the selected or active element. Because the frame, tray, result sticker, spoiler wall and share receipt are all owned by the platform, a new game type changes nothing outside its own tray.
risks: Outline noise: 2px ink on everything can look like a coloring book on dense screens (leaderboards with 10+ rows, admin tables). Mitigation: only containers and keys get ink; rows use --hairline dividers; admin uses flat rows with no lips.

Dark mode is the weaker theme. Black hard shadows vanish (#07050C on bg measures 1.09:1), so dark mode switches to a lighter 'side face' slab (#4A3F66) and per-accent darker lips. This needs eyeballing on a real OLED phone, because the slab can read as a glow if pushed brighter.

Candy accents fail as text on light surfaces (1.4-2.7:1). The 'accent is fill-only, text on accent is ink' rule has to be enforced. Future game authors (including Ashwin at 1am) will be tempted to write text-accent. Add a lint grep or code-review rule banning text-accent.
Pressed-in Done cards could be misread as disabled. They need full-contrast text, the score chip and the 'See results' label. Don't lower their opacity.

The bottom-only lip needs 4px reserved below every key and the diagonal sticker shadow needs 4px on the right. Overflow-x containers (the tab scroller) and the 16px gutters need explicit padding, or shadows get clipped.
Toy-ness can drift childish. Keep chrome neutral (cream, ink, slate), use color only on keys, tiles and stickers, avoid more than one tilted element per screen, and keep Bricolage at 18px or larger.
Three font families add about 130KB. Subset to latin, preload only Figtree, and load Space Mono at 400 and 700 only.
Box-shadow transitions on many keys at once (rollover pop-up) could jank on low-end Android. Cap the stagger and transition only the keys on screen.
directions.buildNotes: 1) src/app/globals.css: replace the :root and dark token values with the hexes above, and add the new tokens. In both themes: --ink: #1E1830, --hit: #3FD68F, --near: #FFD43B, --miss: var(--surface2). --shadow is #1E1830 in light and #4A3F66 in dark. --hairline is color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 14%, var(--surface)) in light and #3A3150 in dark. Declare the derived tokens on ':root, [data-accent]' (inside the dark media query as well): --accent-tint and --accent-lip as defined in scalesToNewGames, plus --key-edge: var(--accent-lip). Gotcha: a custom property that uses var(--accent) is computed where it is declared and then inherited as a fixed value. If you declare it only on :root, game pages that override --accent inline get the root's lemon lip instead of the game's. Extend @theme inline with --color-ink, --color-hit, --color-near, --color-miss, --color-hairline, --color-accent-tint; --radius-key: 12px, --radius-card: 16px, --radius-tray: 20px; --shadow-sticker: 4px 4px 0 0 var(--shadow), --shadow-prize: 6px 6px 0 0 var(--shadow), --shadow-key: 0 4px 0 0 var(--key-edge); --font-display: var(--font-display), --font-num: var(--font-num). Add '@utility key { border: 2px solid var(--key-edge); box-shadow: var(--shadow-key); transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1), box-shadow 180ms cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1); &:active:not(:disabled) { transform: translateY(4px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 0 var(--key-edge); transition-duration: 70ms; transition-timing-function: cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1) } }', '@utility key-pressed { transform: translateY(4px); box-shadow: none }' and '@utility hatch { background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, transparent 0 8px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 6%, transparent) 8px 16px) }'. Add the body dot-grid background and a prefers-reduced-motion block. 2) src/app/layout.tsx: swap Geist/Geist_Mono for Bricolage_Grotesque, Figtree and Space_Mono (weights 400 and 700) with the CSS variables above. Set the themeColor values to #FBF4E6 and #15111D. 3) src/components/ui.tsx: change buttonClass to key variants. accent = 'key bg-accent text-ink', surface = 'key bg-surface text-fg [--key-edge:var(--ink)] dark:[--key-edge:var(--border)]', ghost = 'underline decoration-2 underline-offset-4'. Remove the 'primary bg-fg' variant and active:scale. Use h-12 rounded-key and font-extrabold for all keys. Split Card into Sticker ('rounded-card border-2 border-border bg-surface shadow-sticker') and Tray ('rounded-tray border-2 border-border bg-surface p-4', no shadow). Field becomes h-12 border-2 rounded-key, with focus:shadow-[4px_4px_0_0_var(--accent)] plus a focus-visible outline 2px solid var(--fg) with 2px offset. Avatar gets ring-2 ring-ink and text-ink. Export Key, Tile and Tray for games. 4) src/components/game-card.tsx: add data-accent next to the --accent style. Use the key utility, swapping to key-pressed with bg-surface-2 when finished. Add the tilted emoji tile and the mint '✓ score' chip, and replace text-black with text-ink. 5) src/components/leaderboard-table.tsx: add medallions for ranks 1-3, divide-hairline, font-num points, the highlighter row via bg-[color-mix(in_srgb,#FFD43B_32%,var(--surface))], and the YOU chip. 6) src/app/(app)/page.tsx: add the day meter, the ticket countdown chip and the streak chip, and wrap the standings in a Sticker. 7) src/app/(app)/play/[gameId]/game-host.tsx: wrap GameUi in a Tray. Build the rules sticker with its accent band, the result card as a prize sticker with count-up, the share receipt, and a new SpoilerWall component. 8) src/games/number-hunt/ui.tsx: replace the hard-coded text-sky-600, text-rose-600 and text-emerald-600 classes with tokens (hint text in fg plus ↑/↓ glyphs, and a --hit tile when correct). Use the Key primitive for the Guess button and give rows rounded-[var(--tile-radius)] with border-2. In src/games/number-hunt/logic.ts, change the accent from #f59e0b to #FF8A3D. 9) src/games/registry.test.ts: add the ink-contrast check (7:1 or better) for each accent. 10) The bottom-nav (src/components/bottom-nav.tsx) becomes a floating sticker bar inset 12px above the safe area, with the active tab as a pushed-in lemon pill. In src/app/(app)/layout.tsx, replace bg-bg/90 backdrop-blur in the header with a solid bg-bg, plus a 2px hairline bottom border once scrolled (backdrop-filter is expensive on mid-range phones). No new npm dependencies.

directions.name: Read Receipts
directions.oneLiner: The app is the group chat's sidecar. Each game is a color-themed thread, each result is a message bubble, friends' faces sit at the top of every screen, and the spoiler wall is a sealed message you open by finishing the puzzle.
directions.vibe: Opening the app should feel like opening the group chat right after someone posted a 2/6: you see faces first, then who has already played, then the chance to answer them. Everything social uses chat grammar people already know: right-aligned bubbles for you, left-aligned bubbles for friends with their names in color, centered system pills for events, typing dots for presence, and reaction chips for banter. This makes the rivalry feel personal ("Priya beat you") instead of statistical ("rank 2"). The puzzle itself sits in a plain, still panel with no chat elements inside it, so the chatter stays around the game and never in it.
inspirations: Messenger per-chat theme colors: each game thread carries its own accent the way each chat has its own theme
WhatsApp groups: sender names colored per person, centered date-divider pills, subtle wallpaper behind bubbles, a 1px bottom shadow on light bubbles
iMessage: three-dot typing indicator, tapback-style reactions, bubble grouping with a smaller 'tail' corner
Instagram Stories tray: a row of friend avatars with segmented progress rings at the top of the hub
Discord: presence dots and 'X is playing' status lines
BeReal: you post before you can see your friends' posts, the same mechanic as the spoiler wall
Wordle share-grid culture: the emoji grid is the unit of conversation

typography.notes:
Two families only, both variable, so the payload stays small on mid-range phones. I downloaded both from Google Fonts and checked the 'tnum' feature with fontTools: Bricolage Grotesque has it and Figtree has it. Neither font has tabular digits by default, so every number gets `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` (Tailwind `tabular-nums`). Load them with next/font/google: `Bricolage_Grotesque({subsets:['latin'], axes:['opsz'], variable:'--font-display'})` and `Figtree({subsets:['latin'], variable:'--font-body'})`. Keep `font-optical-sizing: auto` so the opsz axis tightens big numerals by itself.

Type scale:
- Hub greeting: 32/34, Bricolage 800, -0.025em.
- Thread and game names: 17/22, Bricolage 700.
- Big result score: 64/58, Bricolage 800, tabular.
- Leaderboard points: 22, Bricolage 700, tabular.
- Countdown: 15, Bricolage 600, tabular.
- Body and bubble text: 15-16, Figtree 400/500. Inputs are always 16px so iOS does not zoom.
- Sender names inside friend bubbles: 13, Figtree 700, in that person's ink color.
- Timestamps and receipts: 11.5, Figtree 500, muted, tabular.
- Section labels: 12, Figtree 700, +0.06em, uppercase, muted.

Emoji are never web-loaded (Noto Color Emoji is several MB). Share grids use `font-family: var(--font-body), 'Apple Color Emoji', 'Segoe UI Emoji', 'Noto Color Emoji'` at 22px with letter-spacing 2px, so they look the same here as in the real chat.

shape.texture: A chat-wallpaper dot grid on the app background only, drawn on a fixed pseudo-element so it composites cheaply and does not repaint on scroll: `body::before{content:'';position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:-1;background-image:radial-gradient(circle at 1px 1px, color-mix(in srgb, var(--fg) 6%, transparent) 1px, transparent 0);background-size:20px 20px;}`. It flips with the theme automatically because it mixes from --fg. There is no texture inside cards, bubbles or the game panel; those are solid surfaces. Sealed spoiler bubbles use `repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--surface-2) 0 6px, var(--surface) 6px 12px)`.
shape.notes:
Bubbles use 20px radius with one 6px 'tail' corner on the sender's side: bottom-left for friends (`rounded-[20px_20px_20px_6px]`) and bottom-right for you (`rounded-[20px_20px_6px_20px]`). Consecutive bubbles from the same sender get 6px corners on the sender's side, except the last one, which keeps the tail.

Other shapes:
- Cards and thread rows: 20px.
- Game panel: 24px, so it reads as a separate, calmer object.
- Buttons, chips, segmented controls, system pills and date dividers: fully round (999px). The primary button is a 48px-tall pill, like a chat send button.
- Avatars: circles. 28px in bubbles, 40px in lists, 56px in the presence tray.

Borders:
- Decorative borders use --border.
- Input boundaries use a new --border-strong token: light #857F8B (3.88:1 on surface, 3.09:1 on surface-2), dark #77757F (3.75:1 on surface, 3.28:1 on surface-2). This meets WCAG 1.4.11 non-text contrast.
- In light mode, friend bubbles are white surface with the light shadow and no border. In dark mode they are surface with a 1px --border and no shadow.

Measured contrast for the base tokens:
- fg on bg: 15.92 light, 17.02 dark.
- muted on surface: 6.79 light, 7.11 dark. muted on surface-2: 5.40 light, 6.21 dark.
- good on surface: 6.36 light, 9.20 dark. good on surface-2: 5.06 light, 8.04 dark.
- bad on surface: 6.35 light, 7.44 dark. bad on surface-2: 5.06 light, 6.51 dark.
- #141216 on the coral accent: 7.25.

directions.motion:
The vocabulary is chat physics, and only transform and opacity are animated.

- Bubble arrival: from translateY(10px) scale(.94) opacity 0 to rest, 240ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.9,.3,1.15) for a slight pop. transform-origin is the tail corner (bottom-left for friends, bottom-right for you). Lists stagger by 70ms, capped at 6 items so a long thread never takes more than about 0.7s.
- Taps: active:scale-[.97] over 90ms.
- Typing indicator: three 6px dots on a 1.1s infinite loop, each moving translateY(-3px) with opacity .4 to 1, offset 150ms apart. Paused when `document.hidden`.
- Reaction: chip scales 0 to 1.2 to 1 over 260ms. The tray slides up 8px with a fade over 180ms.
- Score reveal: counts up from 0 to the score over 700ms ease-out-cubic using requestAnimationFrame. Tabular figures stop the width from jittering.
- Rank change: FLIP reorder of leaderboard rows over 320ms, cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1). The ▲/▼ delta chip fades in 150ms after the rows settle.
- Unsealing the spoiler wall: the hatch layer fades out and blur(8px) eases to 0 over 360ms, on small bubbles only. The real friend bubbles then arrive in a cascade.
- Date divider at rollover: 200ms crossfade.
- Nothing in the platform animates while a game is in progress. The game panel, header and frame stay still, and only the game's own UI may move.
- Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, everything becomes a 120ms opacity fade, the typing dots become a static '…', and count-ups jump straight to the final value.
directions.soundAndHaptics:
Sounds are off by default, behind a 'Chat sounds' toggle in Profile. They are synthesized with WebAudio, so there are no audio files to download, and the AudioContext is created on the first tap.
- 'Sent' plays when a share succeeds: a 660Hz to 990Hz sine glide over 90ms.
- 'Pop' plays when you add a reaction: 1200Hz, 40ms, fast decay.
- A soft two-note 'ding' plays when a winning result is revealed. Losses get silence, never a sad trombone.

Haptics use `navigator.vibrate`. It works in Android Chrome and is quietly skipped on iOS Safari, which does not support it.
- 8ms when you react.
- 12ms when your result bubble lands.
- [10,60,20] when you move up the leaderboard.

The platform never makes a sound or vibrates during play. Games choose their own feedback.

signatureMoments.design: The button is a full-width 48px pill in the accent with a paper-plane icon, labeled 'Send to the group'. Above it, the bubble shows exactly what will be pasted, rendered as plain text. If navigator.share resolves, a receipt fades in under your bubble: 'Sent ✓✓' in muted 11.5px, plus the 'sent' sound if enabled. If the clipboard path is used instead, the button changes to 'Copied. Paste it in the chat' for 2.5s. The receipt is stored in localStorage per game and day, so it is still there when you reopen the screen. Any failure falls back silently to the clipboard.

Rank changes are computed on the server by comparing today's standings with the previous snapshot. A move becomes a system pill in the hub thread, such as 'Arjun passed you for #1 overall'. Next to it is a 44px '😤' quick-reaction button that opens the share sheet with 'Enjoy it while it lasts @Arjun' as pre-filled banter.

On the leaderboard, rows FLIP-reorder and each row shows a delta chip: '▲2' in good on a 14% good tint (5.17:1 light, 6.94:1 dark) or '▼1' in bad on a 14% bad tint (5.06:1 light, 5.85:1 dark). When you move up you also get the [10,60,20] haptic.

Before you finish, the 'In the thread' section under the game panel shows friends who finished as sealed bubbles. Each one has their avatar, their name in their color, and 'finished 8:02 AM', then a fixed-size 168×44px bubble with the diagonal hatch, a centered 🔒, and 'Sealed until you finish'. The size is fixed so the grid length gives nothing away.

Friends currently playing show a typing bubble instead. Friends who haven't started appear as a muted facepile, 'Not here yet'.

The server returns only the profile and finished_at for sealed rows, never the score, label or grid. On the hub, a thread row's preview says 'Priya, Arjun +2 finished' with a facepile and no outcomes. Each sealed bubble has an aria-label like 'Priya finished at 8:02. Hidden until you finish.'

A Supabase Realtime Presence channel `day:<date>` tracks {userId, gameId} while someone is on a play screen.
- On the hub, that game's thread row swaps its preview to a typing bubble and 'Priya is playing…'.
- The play-screen header subtitle reads '4 of 7 done · Priya playing…'.
- Presence dots are 10px in --good with a 2px ring in the surface color.
- The channel unsubscribes on visibilitychange (hidden) to save battery.
- Without realtime, the app falls back to the in_progress status from the database: 'Priya started 4m ago'.

A horizontally scrolling row of 56px friend avatars, like a stories tray, sits under the greeting. Each avatar ring is a conic-gradient split into one segment per live game, with 3px gaps. A segment is filled with that game's accent once the friend has finished it, and is surface-2 otherwise. The ring is masked to 3px thick with `mask: radial-gradient(farthest-side, transparent calc(100% - 3px), #000 0)`. Badges: 👑 for yesterday's winner, a presence dot for whoever is playing now, and a 🔥 count chip for streaks of 3 days or more. Tapping an avatar opens the profile. You are always first, labeled 'You'.

Each friend result bubble (visible only after you finish) has a 32px '+☺' button at its bottom corner, inside a 44px hit area. It opens a tray of six: 🔥 😂 💀 👏 🫠 🤡. Reaction chips overlap the bubble's bottom edge as small surface pills showing the emoji and count. Only people who finished that game can see them, so reactions can't leak results.

Friends who haven't played get a '👋 Nudge' pill. It calls navigator.share with 'Priya, today's Number Hunt is waiting 👀 <link>', so the poke lands in the real group chat with no push infrastructure.

After 8pm New York time, if you haven't finished all of today's games, a system pill pins under the date divider in the bad color on a 14% bad tint: '🔥 12 on the line · 3:41:10 left'. The countdown is tabular so it doesn't shift.

directions.gameCardTreatment:
Each game card becomes an inbox thread row, a full-width tappable link at least 76px tall, laid out like a chat list:
- Left: a 52px circular 'thread avatar' filled with the game's accent and the game emoji at 26px. An 8px accent unread dot with a 2px surface ring sits top-right when you haven't played today. A partial accent ring around the avatar shows a game in progress.
- Middle: the game name in 17px Bricolage 700 with an optional 'Testing' pill. Under it, a 14px Figtree preview line in muted:
  - before you play, the newest spoiler-safe social event ('Priya, Arjun +2 finished', a typing bubble, or the tagline if nobody has played);
  - after you finish, your own line, 'You: 4/7 · 87', in fg.
  Below that, a facepile of up to four 20px avatars with -6px overlap and a 2px surface ring, plus a '+3' chip.
- Right: a status pill at least 44px tall. 'Play' is a filled accent pill with #141216 text. 'Continue' uses a 14% accent tint with accent-ink text. 'Done' is '✓ 87' on surface-2 in fg, tabular.

Rows sit in one rounded-[20px] surface card divided by hairlines, the way a chat list looks, rather than as separate floating cards. That fits more on screen without scrolling and reads as 'the group's threads'.
directions.leaderboardTreatment:
The leaderboard reads like the group's member list.

Top controls:
- Game tabs: a horizontally scrolling row of 36px pills. Each pill holds the game's emoji avatar and name, and 'All' with 👑 comes first. The active pill fills with that game's accent and #141216 text. Inactive pills are surface-2 with fg text.
- Period control (Today / Week / All-time): a surface-2 pill with a sliding surface thumb (transform transition, 200ms).

Podium: the top 3 appear as a podium of avatars. #1 is 64px with 👑, #2 and #3 are 52px. Each shows the name in its person ink color and points in Bricolage 700 tabular.

Rows (64px tall):
- Rank in Bricolage 700 20px tabular, muted below the top 3.
- 40px avatar with a streak badge ('🔥12' chip).
- Name in 15px Figtree 600, with a subline in muted: '5 played · avg 78'.
- On the right, points in Bricolage 700 22px tabular, right-aligned in a fixed 56px column, so scanning stays fast despite the chat styling.
- A ▲/▼ delta chip.

Your row:
- Styled as an outgoing message: background `color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) 14%, var(--surface))` (fg on it measures 16.03:1 light, 12.23:1 dark; muted 5.95:1 / 5.72:1) and a 'you' pill.
- When your row is off-screen, a sticky 'Jump to you · #5' pill floats above the bottom nav, like 'jump to latest message'.

People who haven't played show muted '–' ranks and a '👋 Nudge' pill instead of points.
directions.playScreenFrame:
The play screen is framed as a chat thread with a calm room in the middle.

Header (sticky, 56px, solid --bg at 95% opacity rather than backdrop-blur, which is cheaper on mid-range Android):
- 44px back chevron;
- 36px game thread avatar;
- game name in 17px Bricolage 700, with a 13px muted subtitle such as '4 of 7 done · Priya playing…';
- a 44px ⓘ rules button.

Before you start, the rules appear as a pinned message from the game: the game avatar plus one left-aligned bubble listing the rules, then a full-width 48px accent pill, 'Start'. During play this collapses to a 36px '📌 How to play' pill that opens a bottom sheet.

Game panel:
- `bg-surface rounded-[24px] border border-border p-4`, with no wallpaper, no shadow, no bubbles and no platform motion inside.
- Games may set `data-bleed` to get p-0 and fill edge to edge, for maps and charts.
- Platform notices such as network errors render as a pill above the panel, never on top of it.
- The platform offers two optional primitives. `<Composer>` is a sticky input bar with a 48px round accent send button, which Number Hunt's guess form already resembles. `<ChatLog>` renders 'you ask, the game answers' bubbles for conversational games (word, number, quote and social games).
- A grid, logic or map game ignores both and gets a plain quiet surface.

Below the panel come your result bubble, then the friends thread, either sealed or open.
risks: The direction's appeal depends on live social features (presence, reactions, nudges, rank-change pills). Shipped as a reskin alone, it becomes 'bubbles around a scoreboard'. Phase 2 (Supabase Realtime Presence plus a reactions table with RLS) needs real backend work.

Color overload: game accents, person colors and emoji all compete. The rule is that person colors appear only on avatar fills and sender names, game accents only on game chrome and your bubble, and the two never share an element. The presence-tray rings are the busiest spot and need a real-device check.
Looking like iMessage or WhatsApp: avoid blue or green outgoing bubbles and copied tail shapes. The coral default and the 20/6 corner geometry are deliberately our own.

Bright accents are fills, not text. On a white surface they measure only 1.58 to 2.57:1, so the accent must never be used as text or as a thin line in light mode. Use --accent-ink. The derived tokens have to be defined in @theme inline, or they resolve against :root's --accent instead of the game's override.

Spoiler leakage: sealed bubbles must be fixed-size and fed by a server query that returns only profile and finished_at. Reactions must stay hidden from people who haven't finished. One careless payload breaks the core rule.
Banter can tip into humiliation in a small group. Losses get neutral copy ('Not this time'), no shame sounds, and system pills celebrate the winner rather than mocking last place.
Chat layouts scan more slowly than tables. That is why the leaderboard keeps a fixed right-hand points column and tabular numerals.
Realtime presence costs battery and data. Subscribe only on the hub and play screens, unsubscribe when the page is hidden, and throttle typing-state updates to one per 10s.
directions.buildNotes:
Phase 1 is the visual system and costs about the same as a full reskin (medium). Phase 2 adds the social backend and is what makes the overall cost high.

PHASE 1

1) src/app/globals.css
- Replace the token values with the ones above.
- Add `--ink:#141216`.
- Add `--border-strong`: #857F8B in light, #77757F in dark.
- Add `--accent-ink-mix`: 38% in light, 100% in dark.
- Add a default `--person:#C4B2FF`.
- Extend `@theme inline` with `--color-ink:var(--ink)`, `--color-border-strong:var(--border-strong)`, `--color-accent-ink: color-mix(in srgb, var(--accent) var(--accent-ink-mix), var(--fg))`, `--color-person: var(--person)`, `--color-person-ink: color-mix(in srgb, var(--person) var(--accent-ink-mix), var(--fg))`, `--font-display: var(--font-display)`, `--font-sans: var(--font-body)`.
- The derived colors must live in `@theme inline`: that way each utility resolves against the element's own --accent and --person overrides rather than :root's.
- Add the wallpaper `body::before`.
- Add v4 utilities: `@utility bubble-them { border-radius:20px 20px 20px 6px }` and `@utility bubble-me { border-radius:20px 20px 6px 20px }`.
- Add `@keyframes bubble-pop` and `@keyframes typing`, plus a `prefers-reduced-motion` block.

2) src/app/layout.tsx
- Swap Geist for Bricolage_Grotesque (axes ['opsz']) and Figtree.
- Set themeColor to #F2EFE9 (light) and #0F1014 (dark).

3) src/components/ui.tsx
- Avatar: pick from a curated PERSON_COLORS by name hash instead of a random hsl, set `--person` inline, render #141216 initials, and add optional props `ring` (conic segments), `presence`, `badge`. The palette is #FF9E80, #FFD166, #7FE0B4, #80C8FF, #F59AD6, #C4B2FF, #B8E66E, #FFB870. Measured: ink on each 9.27 to 12.93:1, names in light mode at least 5.12:1 on surface-2, names in dark mode at least 7.40:1.
- Buttons: rounded-full h-12. The accent variant uses text-ink instead of text-black.
- Field: use border-border-strong and text-base (16px).
- New primitives: Bubble({from, person, name, time}), SealedBubble, SystemPill, DateDivider, TypingDots, Facepile, ReactionChips.

4) game-card.tsx: rewrite as ThreadRow and wrap all rows on the Today page in one divided card.

5) (app)/page.tsx: add the presence tray, the date divider, the countdown in the header, and system pills. Move the top-5 standings below the threads.

6) leaderboard-table.tsx: add the podium, a fixed points column, the delta chip and the viewer-row tint. Add a sticky 'Jump to you' pill using IntersectionObserver. Deltas need yesterday's rank: add a prev-period getLeaderboard call in src/server/leaderboards.ts.

7) Play screen:
- friends-results.tsx becomes a bubble thread.
- LockedResults becomes a SealedBubble list, fed by a new spoiler-safe `finishedBy(gameId, date)` in src/server/plays.ts that returns only profile and finished_at.
- In game-host.tsx, replace the result Card with ResultBubble (score count-up, quoted share grid), relabel ShareButton to 'Send to the group', and add the receipt.

8) Game UIs: replace the raw sky/rose/emerald classes in src/games/number-hunt/ui.tsx with text-accent-ink, text-good and text-bad. Optionally rebuild it on a new ChatLog/Composer pair in src/components/game-kit.tsx.

9) Add registry.test.ts contrast assertions for each game accent.

PHASE 2

10) Supabase Realtime Presence channel `day:<date>`, through a small client hook `usePresence()`.

11) Migration: `reactions(play_id, user_id, emoji, created_at, unique(play_id,user_id))`. The RLS select policy only allows a viewer who has a finished play for the same game and date.

12) Rank-change and system-pill events, derived on the server at render time. No new tables needed.

13) Optional WebAudio sounds module and `navigator.vibrate` haptics, gated by a profile preference.

directions.name: Coin-Op
directions.oneLiner: A pocket high-score cabinet. The machine talks in pixel type, your friends talk in plain type, and each day is a new ROUND.
directions.vibe: It feels like the arcade machine in the corner of a bar where your friends' initials are stuck on the high-score screen and you want yours on top. Dark mode is the cabinet at night: blue-black glass, warm phosphor-white text, and a glow that only shows up at the moments you earn it. Light mode is the printed instruction card on the side of the cabinet: cream card stock, black ink outlines and hard offset "misprint" shadows. It suits a daily friends ritual because arcades were built for rivalry with people you know, short sessions and coming back tomorrow ("CONTINUE?"). The arcade flavour stays in the frame: scores, ranks, initials and status words. The puzzle area itself stays quiet.
inspirations: Galaga / Pac-Man high-score tables: ordinal rank (1ST 2ND 3RD), 3-letter initials, dotted leaders, zero-padded scores
Neo Geo MVS cabinet marquees and the 1UP / HI-SCORE HUD strip across the top of arcade screens
Printed arcade instruction cards and flyers: cream stock, heavy black keylines, slightly misregistered colour offsets
PICO-8 and other fantasy consoles: a small, disciplined palette and a strict grid
Balatro's CRT treatment as a lesson in restraint: the effect sits on the frame and never on the cards you read
Gumroad-style neo-brutalist hard shadows, used for light-mode pressable surfaces

typography.notes: Three voices with strict, checkable rules. (1) PIXEL = 'Press Start 2P' (400 only). It is the machine's voice and draws from a closed vocabulary kept in one ARCADE_COPY map: PLAY, CONTINUE, DONE, START, SHARE, COPIED, LOCKED, CLEAR!, GAME OVER, NEW HI-SCORE, INSERT COIN, READY, 1UP, HI, ROUND n, ordinals 1ST-99TH, 3-letter initials, section headers (TODAY'S GAMES, HI-SCORES), the segmented control (TODAY / WEEK / ALL-TIME) and the hero result score. It is always uppercase and at most 12 characters, and never used for names, game names, sentences or anything user-generated. Allowed sizes are 12/16/24/32/48px (multiples of 4, so 2x-DPR screens render whole device pixels). 12px is the floor, and since the glyphs fill about 7/8 of the em, 12px pixel caps read like 15px sans caps. line-height 1.25, letter-spacing 0.04em at 12-16px and 0 at 24px and up. Always set font-synthesis: none so Tailwind's font-semibold never smears it with faux bold. (2) NUMERIC = 'VT323' (400). Every other number uses it: leaderboard points, averages, streak counts, the countdown, profile stats. It is monospaced, so columns line up without tabular-nums. Minimum 20px because its x-height is small: points 28px, countdown 40px, stat values 36px, line-height 1. Zero-padding (0412) is used only in the HUD, with the leading zeros at muted colour so the real digits stand out. (3) BODY = 'Chakra Petch' (400/600/700). Its chamfered corners echo cabinet bezels while it stays a readable sans. It covers everything a human wrote or that varies in length: player and game names, taglines, rules, forms, errors and, by default, every game UI. Base 15px/1.45, inputs 16px (prevents iOS zoom), greeting 28px/700 with -0.01em tracking, game names on cards 17px/700. Games can opt into .pixel or .num inside their own UI, for example the digit tiles in a number game.

shape.texture: Light mode: a printed score-sheet dot grid on the page background only (not on surfaces): background-image: radial-gradient(circle at 1px 1px, rgb(21 18 31 / 0.07) 1px, transparent 0); background-size: 16px 16px. It is a static paint with no background-attachment: fixed (that is janky on mobile). Dark mode: CRT scanlines on exactly two surfaces, the sticky HUD strip and the result-score panel: background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(to bottom, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.035) 0 1px, transparent 1px 3px). There are no full-screen overlays, no noise and no filters, and textures are never applied inside [data-game-screen]. The spoiler wall uses hazard stripes: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, var(--surface-2) 0 8px, var(--surface) 8px 16px).
shape.notes: Every surface uses a 4px radius, which reads as machined plastic. Initials tiles use 2px and nothing in the system is fully rounded. Borders are 2px everywhere. In light mode the border token is near-black ink, giving the instruction-card keyline look. In-list dividers use border/15 (light) and border/60 (dark) so tables do not get heavy. The ledge shadow (a hard 4px bottom offset, never blurred) appears only on pressable surfaces: game cards, primary buttons and tabs. On :active the element moves translateY(2px) and the ledge shrinks to 2px, like pushing a physical arcade button. Static content cards (result, standings, profile) get the border with no ledge, so pressable and non-pressable are visually different. Form inputs use a 2px muted border (6.98:1 light, 7.49:1 dark), which meets the 3:1 non-text rule even where the dark --border (#4A4970, 2.16:1 on surface) would not. That border is decorative card framing only. Dark-mode 'glow' (text-shadow: 0 0 10px color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 55%, transparent)) has a light-mode twin, the 'misprint' offset (text-shadow: 3px 3px 0 var(--accent)). It is the same emphasis expressed through two kinds of medium (light versus ink) and is used only on the hero score, the 1ST row's points and NEW HI-SCORE.

directions.motion: The motion is mechanical, never springy. Standard UI moves use cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1) at 120-180ms. Anything pixel uses steps() timing so it ticks like hardware. A button press is translateY(2px) with the ledge going 4px to 2px over 60ms linear, releasing over 90ms. Route changes are a hard cut with a 120ms opacity fade on <main> only, because arcade screens cut and it is also the fastest option. Blinks run at 1Hz with steps(2, jump-none) and stop after 3 cycles. The one exception is INSERT COIN, which blinks only while a refresh is in flight. The score count-up runs 0 to final in 900ms, quantized to 30fps with requestAnimationFrame, and holds the final value for 1 frame before the label stamps in. Leaderboard rank changes use FLIP: each row animates from its last-seen position over 280ms with the standard easing. Friends' results on the play screen drop in with a 60ms stagger, at most 5 rows. Only transform and opacity animate, never box-shadow, filter or layout, so mid-range Android phones hold 60fps. There is never any looping or ambient animation while a game is in progress. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, blinks become static, count-up jumps to the final value, FLIP and stagger are off, and only the 60ms press feedback remains.
directions.soundAndHaptics: Sound is OFF by default (people play in bed, at work and on the subway). It is an opt-in 'SOUND: OFF/ON' toggle on Profile, stored as a per-device localStorage preference inside try/catch. There are no audio files. A roughly 60-line sound.ts synthesizes square-wave blips with WebAudio (OscillatorNode type 'square', GainNode peak 0.06, 5ms attack, exponential release): COIN on Start (B5 then E6, 70ms each); CLEAR (C5-E5-G5-C6 arpeggio, 60ms per note); GAME OVER (G4 then D4, 120ms each, falling); SHARE copied (single E6 at 40ms); rank up (two rising notes). Nothing plays on individual keypresses or moves. Where supported, set navigator.audioSession.type = 'ambient' (Safari 17+) so the iOS mute switch is respected. Create the AudioContext lazily on the first user gesture. Haptics use navigator.vibrate, which works on Android and is a silent no-op on iOS Safari: 8ms on PLAY/START, [12, 40, 12] on CLEAR, 30ms on GAME OVER, 10ms on share-copied. Haptics follow the same toggle and are skipped under prefers-reduced-motion.

signatureMoments.design: When the game ends, the game area stays in place and the result card mounts below it and scrolls into view. Timeline: at 0ms the card's 2px border flashes accent for 2 frames. From 120ms to 1020ms the score counts up in Press Start 2P 48px on a scanlined dark panel, in accent-ink with phosphor glow in dark mode and in fg with a 3px misprint offset in light mode. At 1020ms the status word stamps in at Press Start 2P 16px: 'CLEAR!' for a win, 'GAME OVER' for a loss. Under it, the game's native label sits in body 14px muted (e.g. '4/7 guesses'). At 1200ms the share grid fades in at 28px with 0.15em tracking, followed by the SHARE button. If this is a personal best or the top score today, a gold 'NEW HI-SCORE' chip blinks 3 times. On a loss, the line beneath reads 'CONTINUE?' in pixel type with a live VT323 countdown to the next rollover. That turns 'you lost' into the arcade's 'come back', which suits a daily ritual.

A full-width 56px accent button with an ink border and a 4px ledge, labelled 'SHARE' in Press Start 2P 16px with on-accent ink text (12.47:1 on gold). It uses navigator.share where available and the clipboard otherwise. On success the label swaps to 'COPIED ✓' for 1600ms, the share-grid row flashes once (opacity 1, 0.4, 1 over 2 steps) and the optional 40ms E6 blip plays. The share text itself stays plain and chat-friendly: no ASCII art, one header line such as 'Daily · Number Hunt · Round 142 · 87', then the grid. Group chats render emoji, not fonts.

Every day is a 'ROUND n', counted in days since launch and shown as a Press Start 2P 12px muted line above the greeting. The hub countdown card shows 'NEXT ROUND IN' with VT323 40px digits. In the last 60 minutes the digits switch to accent-ink, and in the last 10 seconds the label becomes 'GET READY'. At 00:00 New York time the card reads 'INSERT COIN' blinking at 1Hz while Countdown triggers router.refresh(). When the new data lands, the ROUND number increments with a 1-frame flash and every game card's chip resets to PLAY. If the app is opened after rollover (the common case), there is no modal or splash; the ROUND line shows 'ROUND 143 · READY' and blinks once. After 8pm New York time, if you have not played today, the streak chip turns --bad with 'STREAK AT RISK' in pixel 12px. It is a real nudge with no push notification.

Last-seen rank is kept per board and period in localStorage (as a convenience only, in try/catch).
