ideas.idea: Today the wall is only enforced on /play/[gameId]. The Leaderboard 'Today' tab (the default period) shows a game's result labels and points from getDayLabels/getLeaderboard even if you haven't finished that game. The hub's 'Today's standings' shows summed points, which leak difficulty ('Priya already has 180'). Make one server function the only way any board that includes today is built (like toView is for puzzles). For each friend, show today's points only for games the viewer has finished. Show the rest as a pending dot in that game's accent, with a footnote: 'Excludes games you haven't finished today.'
ideas.why: In a group of 5-20, seeing '2/6' or a big total before you play is the spoiler people complain about in the group chat. A wall with side doors teaches people not to trust it, and the wall is what makes the reveal worth anything.

ideas.area: Spoiler wall: locked state and the reveal
ideas.idea: Replace the generic 🔒 LockedResults card with a teaser that shows who but never how. Use an avatar stack of finishers ('Priya, Sam + 3 finished') and a 'Dev is playing' line from the existing in_progress status, with no scores or grids. On finishing, show your result card first, then let the friend rows come in one by one in score order with your row placed among them: '3rd of 5 so far, 2 still to play'. Respect prefers-reduced-motion with an instant reveal.
ideas.why: The reveal is the reward for finishing. Knowing who finished creates gentle pull ('Sam's already done?') without pressure or spoilers, and a provisional rank gives you a reason to come back later in the day.

ideas.idea: Give the hub explicit day states: fresh, in progress, done, final. While in progress, sort unplayed games first, collapse finished ones into a compact row (emoji, label, score), and make the countdown small or hide it. Once all live games are done, the top section changes into a 'Done for today' summary: day total, provisional overall rank, a 'Share my day' button, and the countdown made prominent ('Next puzzles in 6h 12m', in local time).
ideas.why: A daily ritual needs a satisfying end. An always-visible countdown and a list that looks the same before and after you play make it feel like an endless to-do list. Calling the day done is the anti-chore move.

ideas.area: Share loop into the group chat
ideas.idea: Two changes to shareText and ShareButton. (1) Link to /play/<gameId> instead of window.location.origin, so a friend tapping the link lands on that puzzle (or on login, then that puzzle). (2) Add a combined 'Share my day' message when all games are done: a header line with the date and day total, then one line per game (emoji, label, grid), then the link. Set a share-grid size limit in the game contract (about 10 glyphs per line, 6 lines or fewer) and test it in registry.test.ts so future games don't wrap badly in WhatsApp or iMessage.
ideas.why: The group chat is the real social space; the app's job is to feed it. One clean message a day beats four separate pastes, and a deep link turns every share into a one-tap invitation to play.

ideas.area: Rollover, day close and morning recap
ideas.idea: Midnight in New York is not when most people's day starts, so make the first open of a new day count. Put a 'Yesterday' card at the top of the hub showing the overall winner, each game's top result, where you placed, the closest finish, and the funniest grid. Also close the day early: when the last active player (anyone who played in the last 7 days) finishes, mark the day 'Final' on the boards and lock the ranks. This way a friend who has drifted away can never block it.
ideas.why: This gives people a reason to open the app before they play. The morning verdict ('Sam won by 3') is what friends talk about. A 'Final' state turns 'everyone has finished' into a moment instead of something nobody notices.

ideas.area: Leaderboard structure: week as the unit of competition
ideas.idea: Make 'This week' (Mon-Sun ET) the default leaderboard period and the number shown on the hub. Change All-time from a cumulative-points ranking to a stats table: average score, weeks won (👑 count), best streak. Recommended, but your call as the owner: count each player's best 6 of 7 days in the weekly total, so one missed day doesn't knock you out of the race.
ideas.why: All-time cumulative points reward how long you've been in the group, not how well you play. A friend who joins in month 3 is last forever, and anyone who misses a week stops checking. A weekly reset gives everyone a fresh race every Monday.

ideas.idea: Under the standings, show one line about the person directly above you on the weekly board: '12 behind Sam for 2nd this week'. If you're 1st, show the person below: 'Priya is 8 behind you'. Compute it from spoiler-safe data only. Never compare you with anyone else, and never compare against the whole group.
ideas.why: A small group has natural rivalries, and a single close target is more motivating than a full ranking. It gives you a reason to play the game you'd otherwise skip, and it doesn't single anyone out in front of the group.

ideas.idea: Add a /join/<code> invite link that prefills the code (right now it's typed by hand in signup-form and onboarding-form) and can be posted straight into the group chat. The landing page shows 'Join Ashwin, Priya, Sam + 4 others' with an avatar stack. After signup, go straight to Today with no tutorial; each game's rules panel already explains itself. Existing members see '👋 Rohan joined' on the hub that day. After the newcomer's first finished game, show an 'Add to Home Screen' sheet with iOS steps; it's required for push notifications later.
ideas.why: Friends join because someone shares a link mid-conversation, and every extra step loses them. Showing who's already in is the strongest pull a private group has. Starting with weekly standings means a newcomer can win in their first week.

ideas.area: Streaks: definition and the at-risk state
ideas.idea: Keep the current definition in the streaks() SQL: any one finished game counts for the day. Never require all games. After 6pm local time, if nothing is finished today, show the flame on the hub in an outlined 'at risk' style with calm text: 'Play any one game to keep your 12'. Don't use red, modals or exclamation marks.
ideas.why: Streaks keep people coming back, but only if they feel within reach. Requiring all games turns them into homework. A quiet at-risk cue respects people's evenings and still saves the streak.

ideas.idea: Freezes are earned automatically and computed from play history: every 7 straight days earns one ❄️ (bank up to 2), and a single missed day uses one up without any action. Add this to the streaks() SQL so it returns freezes_banked and frozen_dates, with no stock table to manage, no button, and no way to buy them. Show frozen days as ❄️ in profile history.
ideas.why: One missed day (a flight, a sick day) wiping out a 60-day streak is the most common reason people quit daily games for good. Because the freeze is earned and automatic, it rewards showing up instead of becoming one more thing to manage.

ideas.idea: Add a fixed set of five emoji reactions (🔥 😂 💀 🫡 🤯) on each row in FriendsResults. Only people who have finished that game can see or add them; enforce this on the server. If someone reacts to your result, the hub shows a small notice ('Sam 💀 your Number Hunt'). No text comments.
ideas.why: This brings the group chat's banter into the app at almost no cost and gives finishers something to come back for. A fixed emoji set keeps it playful, avoids moderation, and doesn't compete with the real group chat.

ideas.idea: On Monday, show a recap card on the hub that can also be shared as text. The weekly champion gets 👑 next to their avatar everywhere for the week. Add 3-4 awards computed from the data: Clutch (most solves on the last try, using a result tag the game reports), Steady (lowest score variance), Early bird (first to finish on the most days, from finished_at), Glow-up (biggest gain over their own 4-week average), plus one friendly booby prize. Nobody gets more than one award per week, so they spread around the group. Also include a 'full house' count: how many days that week every active player finished at least one game. It only counts up and never resets.
ideas.why: A weekly story gives the group something to talk about beyond each day's result, and awards for different strengths let people who never win overall still get recognized. A count that only goes up is a shared goal that never puts guilt on the one person who missed a day, unlike a group streak.

ideas.idea: Ask permission only after the app is installed and the person has played on 3 days, never at signup. Send at most one notification per person per day. There are two kinds: (a) a streak reminder at a time the person picks, sent only if they've played nothing that day; (b) an optional 'Day's final: Sam won' sent when the day closes. Never notify at midnight rollover, and never notify each time a friend finishes.
ideas.why: In a friend group, notifications are trusted until they get annoying. One useful reminder saves a streak, and constant notifications get the app muted or deleted. iOS only allows push for installed apps, which is why the install step comes first.

ideas.idea: On /u/[username], add a 'You vs Sam' panel: win-loss-tie record overall and per game, counting only days you both played, plus a strip of the last 10 days. It is computed automatically from play history; there are no challenge or invite features.
ideas.why: In a group this small, most of the fun is about specific pairs of people, like rivalries between siblings or coworkers. Building it from existing data lets it emerge on its own, without creating obligations for anyone.

ideas.idea: When a game moves from testing to live, show a hub banner: 'New: Chart Guess, by Ashwin', with a one-line designer note. For its first 7 days the game is in 'preseason': it has its own leaderboard but doesn't count toward Overall. After the result card, ask a one-tap 'Too easy / Right / Too hard' question and send the answers to admin, so you can tune the game's 0-100 scoring.
ideas.why: You'll be shipping new games regularly. A launch moment turns them into events, preseason stops a badly calibrated new game from distorting the weekly race, and the difficulty votes give you real data instead of guesses.

ideas.idea: Rewrite every empty state so it names a person or an action. 'No one has finished yet' becomes 'You could be first today'. The first finisher sees 'You're first. Results fill in as friends finish', with placeholder avatars. A brand-new profile sees 'Your history starts today'. On the weekly and all-time boards, people who haven't played go into one muted line ('Not played this week: Dev, Mo') instead of ranked rows showing 0 and 'Hasn't played'.
ideas.why: In a small group, empty states are common (early morning, new members, quiet weeks). Generic text makes the app feel abandoned. Ranked zero rows quietly shame specific people in front of their friends.

ideas.idea: Optionally let people play a past puzzle from their profile, never from the hub. Archive plays never appear on any leaderboard, produce no share grid, and are marked 🕰. Mainly for new members and for days someone missed.
ideas.why: It's nice for newcomers, but it weakens the 'everyone plays the same puzzle today' ritual that holds the group together. Keep it clearly second-class and build it only once the core loop is solid.

ideas.idea: Don't include solve time in the 0-100 score and don't show a ticking clock in the game area. If speed appears at all, it's a light weekly award calculated afterwards from started_at and finished_at.
ideas.why: Timers penalize people playing on the commute or in bed and make puzzles stressful instead of calming. They also invite pausing and other gaming of the system, which leads to arguments in a small group.

ideas.idea: Don't build any of these: multiple reminders per day, red notification badges, 'Your streak will DIE' copy, 'nudge Dev' buttons, public lists of who hasn't played, or group streaks that one person can break.
ideas.why: Loss-aversion tactics borrowed from mass-market apps turn a friendly ritual into an obligation and make specific friends feel blamed by name. In a group of 8, that ends with someone quietly leaving.

ideas.area: Anti-pattern: building a social network inside the app
ideas.idea: Don't build in-app chat, comment threads, an activity feed, XP, levels, or piles of badges.
ideas.why: The group chat already exists and is better at conversation. A second inbox and progress systems that only go up add noise, moderation work and maintenance without making anyone want to open the app tomorrow. Put the effort into the share message and the morning recap instead.

platformPrimitives: Server: getVisibleStandings(viewerId, scope, period, date) in src/server/leaderboards.ts, the only way any board that includes today is built. For each friend it hides today's points for games the viewer hasn't finished and returns them as 'pending'. Use it on the hub, the leaderboard and the rival line.
Server: dayProgress(date) returning each user's status per game (not_started | in_progress | finished) with no scores, for avatar stacks, progress dots and the 'Dev is playing' line.
Server: activePlayers(date, windowDays = 7), one shared definition used for closing the day ('Final'), empty states and the 'full house' count.
Hub day state: dayState(viewer) = 'fresh' | 'in_progress' | 'done' | 'final', which decides how the hub is laid out.

Components: <AvatarStack users max={5} /> showing '+N'; <ProgressDots games statuses /> using each game's accent; <LockedResults finishers playing />; <RevealList> with staggered rows and an instant fallback under prefers-reduced-motion; <YesterdayCard />; <RivalLine />; <WeeklyRecapCard />; <StreakFlame state='active'|'at-risk'|'frozen' count />.

Share: shareGameText() linking to /play/<gameId>, and shareDayText() for the combined day message; a share-grid size limit in the GameDefinition docs (about 10 glyphs per line, 6 lines or fewer) checked in registry.test.ts.

GameDefinition additions: optional resultTags(state) => string[] (e.g. 'last-try', 'perfect') for awards to use without game-specific code; optional designerNote; optional preseasonUntil: PuzzleDate, which leaves the game out of Overall.
SQL: extend streaks() to also return freezes_banked and frozen_dates[], computed from play history (1 freeze per 7 straight days, bank up to 2), with no stock table.
SQL: weekly_leaderboard(week_start, best_n = 6) and weekly_awards(week_start) returning (award, user_id, value). Enforce one award per person in TypeScript.

DB: reactions(reactor_id, target_user_id, game_id, puzzle_date, emoji) with a unique (reactor, target, game, date, emoji) and a fixed emoji enum. The server only accepts a reaction if the reactor has finished that game on that date.

DB: profiles.timezone (for local-time countdowns, the 6pm at-risk cue and reminder times); push_subscriptions; notification_prefs(reminder_local_time, kinds[]); difficulty_votes(user, game, date, vote).

Push: service worker plus VAPID web push, and an hourly Vercel cron sender that enforces at most 1 notification per user per day. The permission prompt is only offered when the app is installed and the person has played on 3 or more days.
Route: /join/[code] prefilling the invite code and showing an avatar stack of current members; an iOS 'Add to Home Screen' instruction sheet shown after the first finished game.
Tokens (style-independent names, each checked against WCAG AA in light and dark): --streak, --streak-at-risk, --freeze, --crown, --status-done, --status-playing, --status-locked, --reaction-bg.

ideas.idea: Add a focus-mode <GameScreen> shell for /play/*. It drops the app's sticky brand header and the fixed bottom nav. In their place is a 100dvh grid with 4 regions. (1) A 48px header: back, emoji+name, a status chip ("3/7 left", or the clock for timed games) and a ⋯ menu with How to play, High contrast, Reduce motion and Haptics. (2) A message slot that overlays the top edge of the board, so messages never shift the layout. (3) The board: flex-1 with container-type:size, sized with min(100cqw,100cqh) so it never scrolls. (4) A controls dock at the bottom whose height the game declares, with padding-bottom env(safe-area-inset-bottom). After finishing, a result sheet replaces the controls dock. The shell also sets overscroll-behavior:contain and touch-action:manipulation.
ideas.why: Today the play page sits inside the app layout: sticky header plus fixed BottomNav plus pb-[6rem]. On a 667px-tall iPhone SE that uses about 170px before a 3-row keyboard (~190px) even starts. The board gets squeezed or scrolls, and the nav sits right under the keyboard's bottom row, so a slightly low tap leaves the game. touch-action:manipulation stops double-tap zoom on fast repeated taps. overscroll-behavior stops Android pull-to-refresh firing in the middle of a drag.

ideas.idea: The platform provides <GameKeyboard layout="qwerty"|"numeric"|keys[] keyState={…}/> plus a useGameKeys() hook that maps a physical keyboard on desktop. Games with discrete symbols never use native inputs. Keys are 56px tall with fluid width (a 10-column QWERTY at 360px gives keys about 30px wide). The 6px gutters are padding inside each button, so the gaps are tappable and there are no dead zones. Letter keys fire on pointerdown so they feel instant. Enter fires on click, so sliding off the key cancels it. Backspace repeats while held. keyState colors and marks the keys, so the keyboard itself carries information. Migrate Number Hunt to the numeric layout.
ideas.why: Number Hunt is the "copy this folder" reference game, so whatever it does becomes the convention. It uses <input type=number autoFocus>, which causes three problems. iOS ignores autoFocus, so the player has to tap first. When the native keypad opens it covers the guess list and the error message rendered below the form. It also resizes the visual viewport, which makes the layout jump. A custom keyboard is predictable on every phone and can show per-key state.

ideas.idea: Add an `fx` object to GameUiProps: fx.invalid(msg, el?), fx.accepted(), fx.hit(), fx.solved(), fx.failed(), fx.select() and fx.announce(text). Games never call navigator.vibrate or write their own shake. The host maps each event to motion, haptic, sound (later) and an aria-live message, the same way in every game. invalid = a 6px row shake over 320ms, the message in the slot for 1800ms and the 'reject' haptic. It does not clear the input, so the player edits rather than retypes. Rejected moves never use up a turn (applyMove already supports this).
ideas.why:
Feedback feel then lives in one place: the same shake, the same timing and the same reduced-motion and colorblind handling in Number Hunt and in every future logic grid or map game. Today Number Hunt shows errors in a

under the form, using hardcoded rose-600/400 rather than tokens.

ideas.idea: Add state tokens --state-hit/-near/-miss, each with an -fg pair, and a <Tile state> component that always draws a shape marker as well as the fill. hit = filled + corner dot, near = filled + dashed inner ring (or corner notch), miss = flat with no mark. The states are ordered by lightness so they still read in grayscale. Light: hit #1b6b45 / fg #ffffff (6.49:1), near #c98516 / fg #1c1a17 (5.66:1), miss #d9d4cc / fg #1c1a17 (11.77:1). Luminance 0.11 / 0.29 / 0.66. Dark: hit #5cc98f / fg #0f0e0d (9.37:1), near #b97f14 / fg #0f0e0d (5.61:1), miss #3b3834 / fg #f4f2ee (10.43:1). Luminance 0.46 / 0.26 / 0.04. A high-contrast set under [data-contrast=high] uses orange/blue: light hit #c2410c / white 5.18, near #7cb8f2 / #1c1a17 8.26; dark hit #f5793a / #0f0e0d 7.05, near #2f6fb8 / white 5.14. Replace number-hunt's sky/rose/emerald with these tokens.
ideas.why: I checked these hex values. Even after tuning, neighboring states contrast only 1.4 to 2.1:1 against each other, and Wordle's own orange/blue pair is 1.42:1. Color alone cannot carry the difference, so the shape marker is required, not decoration. Every text pair passes AA. In a group of 5 to 20 that is mostly men, expect about one colorblind member (roughly 8% of men), and that person is 5 to 20% of your leaderboard.

ideas.idea: 1) Have the game page set --on-accent automatically to whichever of #000 or #fff contrasts more with the game's accent, and stop hardcoding `text-black` on accent buttons. 2) Add an --accent-text token for when the accent is used as text: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent), var(--fg) 45%), verified by a test. 3) Fix the base text tokens game screens use. --muted #77716a is 4.43:1 on --bg, which fails; change it to #6b655e (5.28 on bg, 4.88 on surface-2). Split good and bad into fill and text tokens: --good-text #15803d (4.60) and --bad-text #b91c1c (5.94). The current #16a34a is 3.02 and #dc2626 is 4.43. 4) Add a registry.test.ts check that each game's on-accent is at least 4.5:1 and the accent against bg is at least 3:1 (the non-text minimum) in both themes.
ideas.why: Ashwin will choose arbitrary accents for future games. Amber #f59e0b with black text is 9.78:1 and violet is 4.83, but a blue game such as #2563eb with black text is 4.06 and fails, where white would give 5.17. The rules bullets use `text-accent`, and amber on --bg is 1.97:1. "Guesses left" uses text-muted, which fails AA today. A CI test catches a bad accent before friends ever see it.

ideas.idea: Hide the server round trip inside the motion instead of waiting for it. The solution never reaches the client, so results can't be shown optimistically. On submit, the row locks right away and does a 90ms press-in. The reveal (280ms flip per tile, 90ms stagger) starts when the response arrives. A spinner appears on the row only if the response takes more than 600ms. Cheap checks that use only public rules run on the client first, so an invalid guess shakes instantly while the server still re-validates. Examples: out of range, already guessed, not in the word list (shipped as an immutable cached asset). Keystrokes typed during a reveal are buffered, not blocked. The board is never dimmed while a move is pending.
ideas.why: Every move currently waits on a server action, roughly 150 to 600ms on Supabase. An invalid-word shake that arrives half a second late feels broken. Without the dimming rule, the board would flicker on every move.

ideas.idea: The platform owns the finish sequence and delays the spoiler wall until it ends. (1) The game plays its final-move reveal (at most 1.2s) and calls revealDone(). The host forces it after 2s so a buggy game can't stall. (2) A 300ms pause on the final board, with a small settle pop if solved. (3) A ResultSheet slides up over 240ms: the game's own label first ("3/7"), then the 0 to 100 points counting up over 600ms ease-out. (4) The Share button gets focus. (5) The spoiler wall lifts: the lock card turns into the friends list, rows staggered 40ms apart, with a line like "2nd of 5 so far today". Tapping anywhere skips to the end. A loss gets the same calm sequence ("Not this time" plus the reveal). Reopening a finished game later shows the final state with no sequence.
ideas.why: Today the finish is not staged. submitMove calls refresh() on finish, so the friends list replaces the LockedResults card in the same paint where the result card appears under the board. Your own result and your friends' results compete for one moment, and any final animation from the game is cut off. In a friend-group app, the moment you see how everyone did is the payoff, so it should come last.

ideas.idea: Add `timing: "untimed" | "scored"` to GameDefinition. Untimed games show no clock anywhere: not during play, not in the result, not on profiles. Scored games say on the Start panel: "The clock runs from Start until you finish, even if you close the app." The header shows a quiet tabular-nums mm:ss in --muted, with no milliseconds and no red flashing near the end. Only scored games need the Start gate, because it protects the clock. Untimed games can show the board right away and start on the first move (soon).
ideas.why: The server already computes elapsedMs as now minus started_at, a wall clock. The UI should state exactly that rule. A visible timer in an untimed puzzle adds stress and invites comparisons on something that doesn't score, which works against the calm-puzzle goal.

ideas.idea: Do not build pausable timers or 'active time' tracking that relies on heartbeats or visibility.
ideas.why: Pausing across devices can't be enforced: pause, look the answer up on a second phone, resume. Heartbeat-based active time is easy to game and drains battery. In a small private group, a dispute like "he paused it" damages trust in the leaderboard more than any friction does. Use an honest wall clock plus a clear disclosure. If a game needs pausing to be fair, it shouldn't be timed.

ideas.idea: Make two kinds of state official. Committed moves live on the server, sync, and use the existing version/`stale` mechanism. Scratch state stays on each device: unsubmitted letters, pencil marks, selection. Games read and write it through scratch.get/set/clear, stored in localStorage under user:game:date, wrapped in try/catch, never scored, and cleared at rollover. On visibilitychange or focus, the host re-fetches the view. If the version moved on, the message slot says "Picked up from your other device" and re-applies scratch if it's still valid. Leaving mid-game never shows a "Are you sure you want to leave?" confirm, because state is already saved.
ideas.why: People start on the phone at breakfast and finish on a laptop at work. Today a tab left open simply gets a 'stale' rejection on its next move. Scratch state is needed by any keyboard or grid game; without it, half-typed input is lost on every app switch.

ideas.idea: In the last 10 minutes before midnight New York time, show a countdown pill in the play header ("Ends in 9:12"). If a move comes back as day_over, replace the board with a clear card, "Yesterday's puzzle closed while you were playing. Today's is ready", and a button, instead of a bare error notice. On the server, consider a short grace window that accepts moves for day D until 00:05 if the play started on D.
ideas.why: Rollover is at NY midnight, so friends in London (5am) or on the West Coast (9pm) will sometimes be mid-game when it happens. day_over currently appears as a generic notice.

ideas.idea: Define motion tokens in @theme for every game to share. Durations: --dur-press 90ms, --dur-fast 150ms (color and state changes, message in), --dur-base 240ms (sheets), --dur-flip 280ms with --stagger 90ms, --dur-shake 320ms, --dur-count 600ms, --dur-celebrate 900ms max. Easings: --ease-out cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), --ease-in-out cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1), and --ease-pop cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1), used only for settle and success. Expose them as Tailwind v4 --animate-shake, --animate-flip, --animate-pop and --animate-settle, with the @keyframes in globals.css. Rules: animate only transform and opacity, and any single move's full sequence lasts at most 1.2s.
ideas.why: Shared timing is most of what makes different games feel like one product. Limiting animation to transform and opacity keeps mid-range Android phones smooth while 30 tiles flip.

ideas.idea: Under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), or html[data-motion=reduce] set from the ⋯ menu and saved per device, set movement durations to 0. The flip becomes a 120ms color cross-fade. The shake becomes a 2px --bad-text outline pulse plus the message. The score shows its final value with no count-up. Sheets fade instead of sliding. The order of information stays exactly the same; only the timing collapses.
ideas.why: Most people never turn on the OS setting, so an in-app switch matters. Keeping the same order means a reduced-motion player still gets 'my result, then my friends'.

ideas.idea: Define 5 haptic patterns, fired only through fx.*: select 8ms (drag pick-up and drop), hit 12ms, reject [20,60,20], solved [15,70,15,70,40], failed 90ms. Feature-detect 'vibrate' in navigator. On iOS, hide the haptics toggle entirely rather than show one that does nothing, and don't use the iOS <input switch> haptic hack. Haptics default on where supported. No haptic on every keypress.
ideas.why: Android's vibrate is coarse and slightly delayed, so per-key buzzing feels cheap and drains battery. A few meaningful buzzes (rejected, solved) add feel. iOS Safari has no Vibration API, so a toggle there would mislead.

ideas.idea: Sound off by default, with one toggle in the ⋯ menu. If it's built, synthesize short blips with Web Audio (no audio files to download), set navigator.audioSession.type='ambient' where supported so the iOS silent switch is respected, and drive it from the same fx events.
ideas.why: People play in bed next to a partner, in meetings and on commutes, so sound that is on by default gets the app muted or uninstalled. It's a nice-to-have, not part of the core.

ideas.idea: Provide a usePointerDrag primitive for future logic, map and chart games. It uses pointer events with setPointerCapture and an 8px movement threshold before a drag starts. touch-action:none goes only on draggable elements, never on the whole board. Drop-target highlights must reach at least 3:1 against bg. Every drag must also be possible as tap the item, then tap the destination (WCAG 2.5.7). Long-press is never the only way to do something. The board sets -webkit-touch-callout:none and user-select:none.
ideas.why: Drag on mobile web is where homemade games break: page scroll gets stolen, iOS shows the magnifier or callout, and fingers that miss slightly drop items in the wrong place. Tap-tap is also faster for many people.

ideas.idea: The shell provides one polite aria-live region (fed by fx.announce) and a --focus ring token: a 2px outline in --fg with a 2px offset, 15.9:1 on bg. Each game supplies board semantics: role=grid, a label per cell ("Row 2, A, right spot"), arrow-key movement in grids, and Enter/Backspace on desktop. Each move's result is announced as one sentence.
ideas.why: This is realistic for a small group. Desktop keyboard play (friends at work) and colorblind support matter now. Full screen-reader quality can follow, but the contract has to exist before the third game, or every game will need retrofitting.

ideas.idea: Share-grid rules enforced by a registry test against a generated sample: at most 8 emoji per row (so it doesn't wrap in iMessage or WhatsApp on a phone) and at most 6 rows. Only emoji from a platform allowlist (🟩🟨⬛⬜🟧🟦🟥🟪✅❌⬆️⬇️…), with no ZWJ sequences that look different on iOS and Android. In high-contrast mode, share 🟧🟦 instead of 🟩🟨. The ResultSheet shows a literal preview of exactly the text that will be pasted.
ideas.why: The group chat is where the app actually lives. A grid that wraps or shows broken glyphs on a friend's Android phone looks broken there, and the author never sees it.

ideas.idea: An admin page at /admin/sandbox/[gameId]: render GameScreen from any puzzle and state fixture, at 360×640 and 390×844 frames. Toggles for dark, high contrast and reduced motion, plus a slow-network switch that delays submitMove by 800ms. A 'replay finish' button runs the reveal sequence again. Moving a game from testing to live means passing this page's checklist.
ideas.why: Ashwin will keep designing new games of new kinds. This page is where the conventions actually get applied, without playing the real daily puzzle (and spoiling it) to test a layout.

ideas.idea: Do not build confetti or particle libraries, full-screen win takeovers, streak-loss guilt modals, or a different, harsher sequence for losses. The most celebration allowed is one settle pop on the solved board.
ideas.why: For a calm daily puzzle, the reward is seeing how friends did, not particles. Confetti libraries add JavaScript and frame drops on mid-range phones, and guilt modals turn a friends' ritual into a retention mechanic.

platformPrimitives: <GameScreen> shell: header (48px: back, emoji+name, status chip, ⋯ menu), MessageSlot overlay, board (container-type:size, fits without scrolling), controls dock (game-declared height, padding env(safe-area-inset-bottom)), ResultSheet in place of controls. Hides app header and BottomNav on /play/*.
<GameKeyboard layout="qwerty"|"numeric"|keys[] keyState onKey/>: keys 56px tall, 6px gutters implemented as hit-area padding, pointerdown for letters, click for Enter, Backspace repeats while held
useGameKeys(handler): physical keyboard on desktop, ignores modifier keys, with the same key events as GameKeyboard
GameUiProps.fx: invalid(msg, el?), accepted(), select(), hit(), solved(), failed(), announce(text). The host maps these to motion, haptics, sound and aria-live.
GameUiProps.revealDone(): the game signals its final reveal is done; host forces it after 2000ms
GameUiProps.scratch: get/set/clear, unscored state per device, stored in localStorage under user:game:date, cleared at rollover
GameUiProps.prefs: { reducedMotion, highContrast, haptics, sound }, read-only for games
<Tile state="hit"|"near"|"miss"|"empty"|"pending"> with a required shape marker (dot / dashed ring / none) on top of the color

State tokens: --state-hit #1b6b45 / -fg #ffffff, --state-near #c98516 / -fg #1c1a17, --state-miss #d9d4cc / -fg #1c1a17 (light); --state-hit #5cc98f / -fg #0f0e0d, --state-near #b97f14 / -fg #0f0e0d, --state-miss #3b3834 / -fg #f4f2ee (dark); high-contrast overrides under [data-contrast=high]: light hit #c2410c / -fg #ffffff, near #7cb8f2 / -fg #1c1a17; dark hit #f5793a / -fg #0f0e0d, near #2f6fb8 / -fg #ffffff
Color fixes: --muted #6b655e (light; current #77716a fails at 4.43:1), --good-text #15803d, --bad-text #b91c1c, kept separate from fill tokens --good / --bad
--on-accent (auto-picked black or white) and --accent-text (color-mix with --fg), both set beside --accent on the game page
--focus: 2px outline in --fg with 2px offset

Motion tokens: --dur-press 90ms, --dur-fast 150ms, --dur-base 240ms, --dur-flip 280ms, --stagger 90ms, --dur-shake 320ms, --dur-count 600ms, --dur-celebrate ≤900ms; --ease-out cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1), --ease-in-out cubic-bezier(.65,0,.35,1), --ease-pop cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1)
Tailwind v4 animations: --animate-shake, --animate-flip, --animate-pop, --animate-settle, with @keyframes in globals.css; all collapse under prefers-reduced-motion or html[data-motion=reduce]
Layout tokens: --header-h 48px, --key-h 56px, --key-gap 6px, --controls-h (declared by the game), --safe-b env(safe-area-inset-bottom)
HAPTICS map (Android only, feature-detected): select 8, hit 12, reject [20,60,20], solved [15,70,15,70,40], failed 90
<ResultSheet>: native label, then the 0–100 count-up, a literal preview of the share text, Share button focused
<SpoilerGate revealed>: client-side wrapper that keeps FriendsResults behind the lock card until the finish sequence completes
usePointerDrag({ slop: 8, tapTapFallback: true }) with setPointerCapture and touch-action:none only on draggable elements
