GameDefinition additions: timing: "untimed"|"scored"; controlsHeight; an optional publicValidate(move, puzzle) used for instant client-side rejection (public rules only)

Registry conformance tests in src/games/registry.test.ts: on-accent ≥4.5:1 and accent vs bg ≥3:1 in both themes; share grid ≤8 columns and ≤6 rows using allowlisted single-codepoint emoji; rules ≤4 bullets
/admin/sandbox/[gameId]: fixture state, 360×640 and 390×844 frames, theme / high-contrast / reduced-motion toggles, 800ms latency switch, replay-finish button

scores.rationale: This direction fits a daily habit best. An edition number that goes up every day, a factual standings headline, 'Set by Ashwin' bylines and redaction bars make up a ritual that friends can quote back to each other ('No. 214'), and it is not a gimmick. Because the platform is black and white, each game's spot ink is the only color, so a seventh or twentieth game will not turn the hub into a rainbow. The kit (Cell, LedgerRow, Hatch, chart and map rules) already covers Ashwin's planned genres. The 0.20-0.25 luminance band checks out: I measured all six inks at 0.225-0.247, and ink on the darkest one (#5A7EE0) is 4.9:1. The main product risk is that serif type plus heavy rules feels stuffy to 20-somethings. The emoji, the wry headlines and the redaction humor do have to carry the warmth. The design is quieter than most of the others, but that restraint is what lets it last a year.
scores.contrastProblems: None blocking. fg/bg 15.3:1; muted on surface-2 5.64 (light) and 5.69 (dark); good on light surface-2 5.16. Two things to note: hairlines are 1.4-1.5:1 and decorative only, as the direction acknowledges, and raw vermilion #DA5435 is 3.46:1 on bg, so it must always go through accent-ink for text. Ink on #5A7EE0 and #A06AD4 is about 4.9:1, which passes but has little margin.

scores.rationale: This has the best play frame of any candidate. Games declare their HUD readouts as data, the HIT/NEAR/MISS states are separated by luminance so color-blind players are covered by construction, the platform owns the primitives, and a lint rule enforces 'accent is never text'. It is very calm, and that will hold up for 300 days. The 'one lit key, always the next thing to press' rule also turns the day into a sequence, which is a real piece of ritual design. The weaknesses are on the people side. It reads as a Linear or TE clone, monochrome square avatars remove friend identity, and the warmth depends almost entirely on copy. Making HIT an fg fill breaks Wordle muscle memory. Friends will respect it, but they may not love it.
scores.contrastProblems: Mostly clean (fg/bg 17.1:1). The margins are thin in three places: good #0B7A3E on light surface-2 is 4.55:1, ink #0B0B0C on cobalt #2F7BF5 is 4.94:1 (the tile glyph case), and NEAR (accent) against MISS on light surface-2 is 3.09:1, which only just meets the 3:1 non-text rule.

scores.rationale: It understands that the product is the friend group better than any other direction. The presence tray with per-game ring segments, the 'finished 8:02' sealed bubbles, nudges sent through navigator.share and yesterday's 'won' recap all give strong daily reasons to open the app. The problems: it imitates the group chat it is supposed to sit beside, and copying iMessage grammar invites comparison. Game accents, person colors, emoji and crowns all compete, so it gets busy fast. Bright candy accents need luminance 0.32-0.75, which rules out deep colors for future games. Most of the appeal also depends on Phase 2 realtime work and a reactions table. Shipped only as a reskin, it is 'bubbles around a scoreboard', and the chat grammar (bubbles, typing dots, reactions) may feel gimmicky by month six.
scores.contrastProblems: Accent fills are only 1.58-2.57:1 against white surface, so they must never be text or thin lines in light mode. That depends on accent-ink at a 38% mix. Base tokens pass: muted on light surface-2 5.40, ink on coral 7.25. The presence-tray ring segments in surface-2 against bg are low contrast.

scores.rationale: The face-down to face-up 'dealt a hand' metaphor maps neatly onto the daily state machine (unplayed, in progress, done), and the struck-through old rank on a scorepad is a charming way to show a rank change. 'What the group sees' is a strong share preview. Against that: skeuomorphism (linen, felt, a lamp spotlight, lattice backs, a perforated scorepad, a blue/red ruled margin) gets tiring once the novelty is gone, three variable fonts come to roughly 200-250 KB, and multi-layer shadows over felt noise are a real risk on mid-range Android. Dark-mode green felt also clashes with any green game. Generality is fine because the play mat is plain, but a chart or map game inside a card-table frame feels a little out of place.
scores.contrastProblems: Measured: fg/bg 13.6:1 (light) and 14.6:1 (dark), muted/bg 5.25. The weak spots are ink on #e0614a at 4.92:1 and decorative card borders at 1.6:1 (the shadow carries separation, which fails in flat or forced-colors contexts). Lattice backs need the label plate under any text, and that is enforced only by the component.

scores.rationale: It is fun to touch, and 'Done cards stay pressed in' is the best single glanceable-state idea in the set. Candy accents with a 7:1 ink rule are easy for Ashwin to extend. But 2px ink outlines, lips, sticker shadows, a dot grid, a tilted tile and count-ups everywhere make it the noisiest of the calm-ish directions. The Gumroad/Duolingo neo-brutalist look is familiar by now and will feel dated within a year. Dark mode is clearly weaker: the lilac slab can read as a glow, and per-accent lips must be eyeballed. Bricolage plus three families adds about 130 KB.
scores.contrastProblems: Lemon accent on light surface is 1.4:1 and candy fills range 1.4-2.7:1, so they depend completely on the mandatory 2px outline. The dark tangerine lip is 2.47:1 against bg. The dark border #7E72A6 is 3.8:1 (passes 1.4.11). Text tokens pass: muted on light surface-2 5.84, ink on #FF8A3D 7.29.

scores.rationale: It is personal to Ashwin, and several of its structures carry real data: depth bars as true margin to the leader, deltas from real snapshots, and spoiler-safe totals over finished games, which is an important fix the others mostly miss. 'Yesterday's close' is a good daily hook. Through a product lens, though, it is Ashwin's aesthetic forced onto 5-20 friends who did not choose to play a trading terminal. Tickers, 1D/1W, INDEX and HALTED are homework for non-finance players. Reserving red and green for deltas also takes the most natural game-feedback colors away from future games. The ticker-tape marquee is moving chrome on a hub that should feel calm, and it gets old fast. The cosplay risk is real.
scores.contrastProblems: Light-mode accent fills (amber, lemon #EBD443, silver #A9B8CC) are 1.4-2.0:1 against surface and need an inset accent-ink border. Light bad on surface-2 is 4.92:1 (fine). Black on silver is 10.4:1. Red/green deltas are mitigated by ▲/▼ glyphs.

scores.rationale: It is the most distinctive, and the arcade mechanics (initials, HI-SCORE, a CONTINUE? countdown on a loss, ROUND n, STREAK AT RISK) fit rivalry well. Still, Press Start 2P plus VT323 is a costume that people will be sick of within weeks. Blinking text, 'GAME OVER' on a daily loss, glow and scanlines all go against a calm puzzle ritual. Three novelty fonts with strict size floors (VT323 at 20px or more, pixel type at 12px or more) are fragile on small phones. The closed ARCADE_COPY vocabulary is a clever guardrail, but it shows how easily the look tips into gimmick. Future quote and social games will clash with the arcade frame.
scores.contrastProblems: The dark --border #4A4970 is 2.16:1 on surface, so card edges are effectively invisible. That is acknowledged as decorative, but it is also the ledge color on pressables, so the pressable cue fails 1.4.11. The gold accent is 1.55:1 as text on light surface. VT323's small x-height undermines readability at 20px even though contrast passes. Measured tokens: muted on light surface-2 5.59, ink on #5A7DFF 5.42.

graftIdeas.idea: Edition number (days since the group's EDITION_EPOCH) in the folio and in the share text, plus a template-only factual headline built from data already on screen ('Priya leads by 14; three still to play.'). Each day gets an identity without any AI copy.

Fixed-width solid redaction bars for sealed results instead of blur, with the server never sending the data. Bar length leaks nothing, and the 'SEALED' label makes them distinct from loading skeletons.

A registry.test.ts luminance-band gate (about 0.20-0.25) so one accent hex works in both themes, defining accent-ink with color-mix inside @theme inline so per-game --accent overrides resolve at the element, and a grep test that bans raw Tailwind palette classes under src/games.
'Set by Ashwin' bylines and 'PROOF' labels on testing games, which make Ashwin's role as the game designer part of the product.
Finished games stay visibly pushed in (sunk, no lip, full-contrast text), so what is left to play today shows at a glance.
Games declare HUD readouts as data (label/value pairs) and the platform renders them, so every future game's status bar looks identical and games never style their own status text.
One lit accent per screen: the next-up game's Play key on the hub, then Start, then Share. This turns the daily routine into a readable sequence.

HIT/NEAR/MISS feedback tokens differentiated by luminance, not hue, which makes them color-blind-safe by construction and shared across word, logic, map and number games. Also a 7-cell streak tick strip instead of a flame emoji in the interface.
A presence/progress tray of friend avatars whose ring segments fill with each game's accent as they finish. It is spoiler-safe social pressure and the strongest 'open me' cue in the set.

A 'Nudge' action that calls navigator.share with a prefilled poke, so reminders land in the real group chat without push infrastructure. Sealed rows also show who finished and when (8:02), but not the outcome.

Hub and overall 'Today' totals computed only over the games the viewer has finished (server-side), which closes the spoiler leak the current hub already has. Also a dismissible 'Yesterday's close' recap on the first open each day.
Leaderboard depth bars (points divided by the leader's points), which show the real margin to the leader at a glance.
A 'What the group sees' strip that previews the exact paste text before Share, plus the old rank shown struck through beside the new one, like a scorepad correction.

On a loss, show 'Come back tomorrow' with a live countdown to the next puzzle (Coin-Op's 'CONTINUE?' idea, minus the arcade costume), and after 8pm show a 'streak at risk' line. This turns failure and procrastination into reasons to come back without push notifications.

judges.bestBlend: Broadsheet as the visual system, with Read Receipts' social layer re-expressed in print grammar, and Instrument's play-frame contract underneath. Broadsheet supplies the calm, long-lived base: black-and-white platform, one spot ink per game, edition numbers, headlines, redaction bars, the luminance-gated accents and the game kit. Its weakness is coldness and the lack of live social pull, which is exactly Read Receipts' strength. So graft the presence/progress avatar tray (rings filled with game spot inks, styled as a 'Who's in today's edition' row of monogram avatars), 'finished 8:02' sealed rows, a Nudge action through navigator.share, and the yesterday's-winner recap as a 'Yesterday's final' strip. Leave out the bubbles, typing dots and reactions, which would fight the print look and add Phase-2 realtime cost. Under the hood, take Instrument's readouts-as-data HUD, its luminance-differentiated HIT/NEAR/MISS tokens and its 'one filled primary action per screen' rule for the play frame. Also add Toy Box's sunk Done rows (a done index row recedes onto surface-2) and Closing Bell's server-side rule that hub totals count only the games the viewer has finished. Together this gives a group paper that is calm enough for a year, warm through people rather than decoration, and generic enough for any game Ashwin designs.

scores.rationale: The most coherent system of the seven. The platform is black and white and each game is one spot ink, so color carries a single meaning and the puzzle frame stays calm by design. The 0.20-0.25 luminance band means one hex works in both themes. I checked it: ink on the six game accents measures 4.90-5.29, and the accents as graphics measure 3.34-3.60 on light surface and 4.50-4.87 on dark. It also catches font traps (Libre Franklin has no tnum, so numbers go in Newsreader) and the @theme inline color-mix trap. The edition number, bylines, 'Set by Ashwin', galley 'Proof' and redaction bars give the group real things to joke about without game-show noise, and they suit an owner who sets puzzles. Dark mode is warm charcoal with cream ink (fg/bg 15.06, muted/surface 6.40), not an inverted afterthought. Weaknesses: the newspaper-puzzle-page idea sits close to NYT Games, so it is not fully unique. A serif with heavy rules could feel stuffy to some friends. The platform vermilion and the bad crimson are both reds.
scores.contrastProblems: No failures. Some pairs are tight. On-accent ink on the light platform accent #DA5435 is 4.72 (passes AA, little margin). Game ink on #5A7EE0 is 4.90 and on #A06AD4 is 4.91. Hairline border on surface is 1.50 light and 1.41 dark, which is fine only because the proposal treats it as decorative and puts fg borders on inputs, buttons and the frame. Game accents as fills on light surface are 3.34-3.60: they pass 3:1 for graphics but must never be used as text (the proposal routes accent text through accent-ink).

scores.rationale: The cleanest and calmest system. Graphite with one lit control per screen is a strong rule: the lit control is always the next thing to press. The platform-owned readout strip (games declare HUD values as data) and the HIT/NEAR/MISS vocabulary separated by luminance rather than hue are the best ideas here for hosting arbitrary future games, and the vocabulary is safe for color-vision deficiency. The luminance band (0.20-0.24) works: ink on the six accents is 4.94-5.34, and accents on light surface are 3.69-3.98. Typography (Inter with cv05/cv08 so I and l differ, JetBrains Mono for numbers) is chosen for word puzzles. The trouble is identity. It reads as Linear or Teenage Engineering, and the proposal admits the cold, corporate risk. Monochrome square avatars throw away friend identity, which is the main warm element in a friends' app. Game accent #1 (#EC4F17) is the same color as the platform accent, which defeats the 'one lit signal' meaning.
scores.contrastProblems: Bad on light surface-2 is 4.74, just over 4.5. Border on dark surface is 1.31, decorative only, and it relies on --border-strong (claimed 3.39) for anything interactive. Game accent #1 duplicates the platform accent #EC4F17, a semantic clash rather than a contrast failure. Everything else passes comfortably (fg/bg 17.14 light, 16.77 dark).

scores.rationale: The most personal to Ashwin, and the best dark mode of the set: blue-black with amber (fg/bg 16.62, black on amber 10.88). The rule that only real data gets terminal styling is the right defense against cosplay. Depth bars are true proportions of the leader's score, deltas come from real snapshots, and IBM Plex across three widths is a disciplined, legible family. The problems are in the brand fit and in light mode. A finance terminal is Ashwin's identity, not the group's, and non-finance friends may find it homework-like even with plain-English buttons. The game palette consists of pale, bright colors that nearly vanish on the light surface (lemon 1.43, cyan 1.95, silver 1.93), so every fill needs an inset accent-ink border. Lemon #EBD443 sits close to house amber. Red and green are reserved for deltas, which narrows the color vocabulary for future games. The ticker tape is a moving element that could grate by day 100.
scores.contrastProblems: Light-mode game accents on surface are 1.43 (lemon #EBD443), 1.93-1.95 (silver, cyan) and 2.40-2.41 (the rest). As fills they fail 3:1 for graphics without the inset ink border. The light platform accent #FF9F1C on surface is 1.97. Bad on light surface-2 is 4.92 (OK). Light border on surface is 1.64, decorative. Text pairs pass.

scores.rationale: Charming and functional. The three depth levels each have one meaning (lip = press, offset = sticker, flat = work surface), and 'Done cards stay pressed in' is a great at-a-glance state that needs no copy. It suits a daily fidget ritual. But 2px ink outlines plus hard shadows plus candy fills is the 2021-2024 Gumroad/neo-brutal trend, already widely copied and likely to date. The ink keylines on every container get noisy on dense leaderboards. The proposal admits dark mode is weaker: it swaps the black shadow for a lilac slab (1.94 against bg) and uses per-accent lips, which needs tuning on a real device. Candy accents are fill-only and depend entirely on outlines in light mode. Bricolage plus Figtree plus Space Mono is three personalities. Space Mono for every number feels quirky rather than calm in a puzzle readout.
scores.contrastProblems: The light platform accent #FFD43B on surface is 1.40. Game accents on light surface are 1.38 (#C3E84A), 1.88-1.89 (#5CC6FF, #2FD0C0) and up to 2.31, so all fail 3:1 as graphics and need the mandatory 2px ink outline. The dark border #7E72A6 on surface is 3.80 (passes 3:1). Ink on accents is 7.29-12.18 (excellent). Body text pairs pass (muted on surface-2 is 5.84 light).

scores.rationale: Warm and tactile, with good ideas. Per-game back patterns give each game an identity that does not rely on color alone. Corner indices work like a card's rank over suit. The face-down fan of cards as a spoiler wall works. The palette discipline matches Broadsheet's (luminance band, ink on accent about 5:1). It falls down on craft. Dark mode puts a green felt bg (#0f1d17) under brown-charcoal surfaces, two warm and cool families fighting each other. Light fg/bg is the weakest of the set at 13.64. The type stack (Fraunces SOFT+opsz, Figtree, Recursive CASL+MONO) is about 200-250KB, too heavy for mid-range phones. Every surface carries a texture: linen, felt noise SVG, card-back lattices, scorepad rules, a perforation and a spotlight, so the skeuomorphism will tip toward kitsch over 100 days. A pattern behind every unplayed card makes the hub busy. 'Rank as card' and 'scorepad' also suit a numeric leaderboard better than word, map or quote games.
scores.contrastProblems: The light accent #bf861c on surface is 3.08, barely over 3:1. Ink on game accent #e0614a is 4.92 (passes AA, little margin). Light fg/bg is 13.64, which passes but is below the 15+ that most peers reach. Border on surface is 1.60 light and 1.43 dark, decorative only. The green felt bg against the green game accent #46a058 has a weak hue difference (the proposal admits this).

scores.rationale: The social mechanics (presence tray, sealed bubbles, nudge via native share, reactions only visible after finishing) are product ideas worth keeping. But as a visual brand it borrows chat-app grammar from iMessage, WhatsApp and Messenger, so it looks like a messaging app rather than having its own identity. It adds color sources (bright game accents, person colors and emoji) that compete. The bright accents are fills only and collapse on white. Light-mode accent text needs a 38% mix toward fg to be readable. Much of its appeal depends on Phase 2 realtime work (high cost). As a reskin alone it becomes bubbles around a scoreboard. Chat layouts also scan more slowly than tables for a leaderboard. Pill everything at 20px radius plus a bouncy cubic-bezier overshoot is busier than a puzzle app needs.
scores.contrastProblems: Game accents on light surface are 1.53 (#A6E34B), 1.58 (#FFC53D), 1.88 (#3ED598) and up to 2.30, all failing 3:1 as graphics. The light platform accent #FF7A59 on surface is 2.57. Accent text depends on the derived 38% accent-ink mix. Muted on light surface-2 is 5.40 (OK). The decorative border is 1.49 light and 1.44 dark. Ink on accents is 7.25-12.16 (excellent).

scores.rationale: Memorable and fun on day one, and it is honest about its risks: a closed ARCADE_COPY vocabulary enforced by a type, 12px multiples so pixel glyphs land on whole device pixels, and font-synthesis: none. 'CONTINUE?' with a countdown after a loss is a lovely reframe. But Press Start 2P throughout the chrome (section headers, segmented control, ordinals, status chips) plus VT323 for every number (it needs at least 20px because of its tiny x-height) plus Chakra Petch gives three hard-to-read display voices, and the novelty wears thin fast. That is the definition of poor longevity. Blinking, glow, scanlines and initials tiles accumulate visual noise around the calm zone. The pixel aesthetic does not fit future map, chart or quote games, which must avoid it inside the frame. The dark border fails as a meaningful edge. Arcade styling for a friends' puzzle habit is a costume rather than an identity.
scores.contrastProblems: Bad on light surface-2 is 4.65, borderline. The dark border #4A4970 on surface is 2.16, under 3:1 (the proposal uses a muted border on inputs to compensate). The light platform accent gold #FFC629 on surface is 1.55, so it is fill-only. Game accents on light surface are 3.16-3.55 (passes for graphics). Pixel fonts at 12px and VT323 at 20px are legibility risks even where the ratios pass.

graftIdeas.idea: Fixed-width solid ink redaction bars for the spoiler wall (never blur; the server never sends the data), wiped away with clip-path once you finish. The same bars fill the PTS column on per-game Today boards.

Accent luminance band (about 0.20-0.25) enforced in registry.test.ts. One hex then works in both themes with dark ink text. Derive accent-ink via color-mix inside @theme inline, so per-game --accent overrides re-resolve at the element.
Edition number ('No. 214') in the folio line and the share text, plus 'Set by Ashwin' bylines and 'PROOF' labels for testing games. These frame Ashwin as the puzzle setter.
Games declare HUD readouts as data, e.g. [{label:'GUESS', value:'3/7'}]. The platform renders them, so every game's status looks the same and games never style their own status text.
HIT/NEAR/MISS/EMPTY state vocabulary separated by luminance, not hue. It is safe for color-vision deficiency and works for word, logic, map and chart games.
The 'one lit control per screen' rule: the accent fill moves from Play to Start to Share and is always the next action.
Day-progress hairline under the countdown, plus a 7-cell streak tick strip instead of a flame emoji in the UI.
A right-anchored depth bar behind each leaderboard row showing points as a fraction of the leader's points. It is real data rather than decoration and shows the gap to the leader at a glance.
Today's overall totals on the hub and in the HUD are computed only over games the viewer has finished, which closes the existing spoiler leak (Coin-Op flags the same leak).

Done cards visually 'settle' (pressed in, or quieter), and unplayed ones stand out, while keeping full text contrast. Pair this with a 'day meter' that has one slot per game, filled with that game's accent.
An optional per-game backPattern (stripes, dots, chevrons) hashed from the game id, so games are never told apart by color alone once there are more than 6.
'Nudge' a friend who hasn't played via navigator.share with a pre-filled message, so the poke lands in the real group chat with no push infrastructure.
The sealed spoiler row shows who finished and when (avatar plus a 'finished 8:02' timestamp). This adds social pressure without revealing results.
After a loss, show 'Come back tomorrow' with a live countdown to the next puzzle, so a loss leads into tomorrow's game instead of ending on failure.
Games call a single platform feedback('tap'|'solve'|'fail') rather than audio or vibrate directly, so haptics and sound stay consistent and respect the toggles.

judges.bestBlend: Broadsheet plus Instrument. Use Broadsheet as the brand: the black-and-white ink platform, games as single spot inks within the 0.20-0.25 luminance band, Newsreader for titles and all numbers, Libre Franklin for UI, the rule system, the edition number, bylines and redaction-bar spoilers. Its warm paper and charcoal tokens are the strongest light/dark pair. Graft on Instrument's structural discipline: the one-lit-control-per-screen rule (with game spot inks as the lit fill), data-declared HUD readouts rendered by the platform above the puzzle frame, the luminance-separated HIT/NEAR/MISS/EMPTY state vocabulary inside Broadsheet's kit, the day-progress hairline under the folio countdown, and the 7-cell streak tick strip as the 'RUN 12' detail. Add Closing Bell's depth-to-leader bar as a faint hairline-height bar in the agate rows, and its rule that hub totals count only finished games. Drop Instrument's monochrome avatars (keep Broadsheet's low-chroma oklch monograms) and its duplicated orange accent. The result has a clear editorial identity with an instrument-grade calm inside the puzzle frame.

scores.rationale: The strongest engineering proposal. It loads two variable fonts at about 87 KB, and its glyph claims were checked with fontTools: Newsreader has tabular digits by default and Franklin has no tnum, so it adds a grep test that every number uses font-num. It defines derived accent tokens correctly inside @theme inline, so color-mix resolves on each element and follows a game's --accent override. A luminance-band unit test (0.20–0.25) lets one hex work in both themes, and I confirmed all six inks fall at 0.225–0.247. Elevation is flat, so there are no shadow layers to paint, and motion only uses transform, opacity and clip-path. The grain PNG is about 4 KB and appears in light mode only, never inside the frame. It is the most complete answer for hosting future games: a Kit with Cell, Key, LedgerRow and Hatch, explicit rules for charts, maps and quotes, and state shown by shape as well as color. Fixed-width redaction bars, with real data never sent to the client, are the cleanest spoiler wall in the set. I measured fg/bg at 15.3 light and 15.1 dark, muted at 5.6 or better everywhere, and good/bad at 5.2 or better on surface-2. Weaknesses: serif plus rules could feel stuffy for a friends' game, and the masthead, edition and headline templates add about a day of chrome work. The 1px hairlines are about 1.4:1, which is fine only because they correctly limit them to decoration.
scores.contrastProblems: No text failures. The platform accent #DA5435 is 4.72:1 against ink #14120E. That passes AA, but it is below the '≥4.9' figure they quote, which is true only for the six game inks. Accent as a graphic on light bg is 3.46:1, which passes. Hairline borders at about 1.4:1 are decorative only, as they state.

scores.rationale: The easiest to build and maintain. The game accent is never used as text, and on-accent text is always the fixed ink #0B0B0C, so there are no derived color-mix tokens and no var-inheritance trap. The luminance band 0.20–0.24 is enforced by a test, and I measured ink on all six accents at 4.94–5.34. The best generality idea in the whole set is that games declare HUD readouts as data and the platform draws them, so no game ever styles its own status text. HIT, NEAR and MISS differ by luminance rather than hue: 15.8:1 for hit vs miss, and 3.09–3.33 for near vs miss. That makes them safe for color-blind players by construction. The primitives (Tile, Cell, Key, Keyboard, Meter, ChoiceList, Readout) cover every planned genre. It also offers a 'one accent fill per screen' rule, ScoreRoll and a FLIP done with WAAPI and no library. The font cost is about 100 KB, and it can drop to two families. It is the least distinctive option: it reads as a Linear clone, and its warmth depends on copy. HIT as a solid black tile breaks Wordle habits. Mono tiny caps at 11px are at the edge of legibility. The dot grid risks moiré on low-DPI screens.
scores.contrastProblems: Light bad on surface-2 is 4.74:1, a narrow pass. NEAR vs MISS is 3.09:1, right at the 1.4.11 floor. Otherwise fg/bg is 17.1 light and 16.8 dark, and muted is 5.6 or better. None fail.

scores.rationale: Its depth rules are honest and consistent: a lip means you can press it, an offset means a static sticker, and flat means a work surface. Done cards stay pressed in, a state you can read at a glance. Redeclaring derived tokens on ':root, [data-accent]' works, provided every override also sets data-accent. That makes it a convention one developer has to remember on every new component. Costs: three font families (about 130 KB), 2px outlines and hard shadows on every key and container, and box-shadow transitions on lips. Many keys springing back at rollover could stutter on low-end Android. Lips and shadows also need reserved padding in every overflow container. Candy accents are fills only, at 1.3–1.4:1 on light paper, so the mandatory 2px ink outline and a ban on text-accent have to be enforced forever. The dark theme depends on a hand-picked side-face slab colour, which they admit needs checking on a real OLED phone. Bricolage at 18px or larger and the tilted stickers should wear well over the first weeks, but outline noise on dense boards could start to grate by day 100.
scores.contrastProblems: The lemon platform accent #FFD43B is 1.40:1 on the light surface and 1.30:1 on bg. All light-mode accent fills are 1.4–2.7:1 and depend on the outline. The dark key lip at 2.47:1 on bg is decorative. No text failures: muted is 5.8 or better and the dark border is 3.8:1.

scores.rationale: The most data-honest proposal. Depth bars show real proportions to the leader, deltas are always arrow plus sign, and it spots the real spoiler leak in hub totals that needs a server-side filter. IBM Plex Mono gives clean tabular numbers. Costs: seven static font files (about 120 KB), a CSS marquee that needs IntersectionObserver and visibility pausing, sparklines that need a new server query for daily history, and previous-period leaderboard calls. It has an unacknowledged token bug. The build notes declare `--accent-ink: color-mix(... var(--accent) ...)` as a root custom property and map it through @theme inline as var(--accent-ink). That resolves against :root's amber, so game pages would get amber ink rather than their own colour. Light-mode amber and lemon fills are 1.8–2.0:1 and need an inset ink border on every accent control. Game accents are not held to a luminance band by a test, only by a fixed palette. The trading metaphor fits Ashwin but risks feeling like homework, or like costume, for friends who don't trade. A ticker scrolling every day will tire.
scores.contrastProblems: The platform amber #FF9F1C is 1.97:1 on the light surface and 1.80:1 on bg, so every fill needs the inset ink border. Light bad on surface-2 is 4.92:1. Lemon #EBD443 has about 13° of hue separation from the house amber. --accent-ink on :root will not follow per-game overrides unless it is moved into @theme inline. There are no hex-level text failures.

scores.rationale: Warm and tactile, and it has one excellent generality idea: a backPattern per game, hashed from the game id, so games never depend on colour alone. Engineering cost is the worst of the medium-cost options. Fonts are Fraunces with SOFT and opsz axes plus Figtree plus Recursive with CASL and MONO, about 200–250 KB by its own estimate. That is too heavy for mid-range phones on cellular. It also needs a feTurbulence SVG felt texture, a fixed spotlight pseudo-element, three-layer shadows on six or more cards, half-flip 3D animations with cleanup, a card-back lattice behind label plates, perforation and margin-line gradients, and View Transitions. Derived tokens rely on a manual `.accent-scope` class on every element that sets --accent, an easy one to forget. The platform accent changes between modes (#bf861c and #e2ad45), which goes against 'one hex both themes'. Shared primitives such as Tile, Slot and Feedback help, but the card metaphor works best for word and number games. Map and chart games get only generic guidance. Skeuomorphic texture tends to wear thin over 100 days.
scores.contrastProblems: The platform accent #bf861c is 2.50:1 on light bg, so a Play tile edge sitting on the tablecloth fails the 3:1 non-text rule unless the shadow or edge carries it. Card edges at about 1.6:1 are intentionally low contrast. fg/bg is 13.6:1 in light, still above 7. Ink on palette accents is 4.92–5.46, which passes.

scores.rationale: The best fit for the social side of the habit: nudges through navigator.share, typing presence, and a spoiler-safe `finishedBy` query that returns only profile and finished_at. Engineering cost is high, though. It needs Supabase Realtime Presence, a reactions table with RLS, and server-computed rank events. Its own risk list admits that without phase 2 it is only bubbles around a scoreboard. Performance problems: an infinite typing-dots loop, conic-gradient avatar rings with masks for every friend, and a filter: blur(8px) unseal animation, which is exactly the kind of filter animation mid-range phones handle badly. The chat grammar does nothing for logic grids, maps or charts; those fall back to a plain panel, so the system's identity disappears for spatial games. Bright candy accents (luminance 0.36–0.64) cannot be text in light mode, which brings in --accent-ink-mix and person-ink derived tokens. Bubble geometry also has to steer clear of looking like iMessage or WhatsApp.
scores.contrastProblems: The coral platform accent #FF7A59 is 2.57:1 on the light surface and 2.24:1 on bg, and game accents are 1.6–2.6:1. They are fills only and must never be used as text or thin lines. Light bad on surface-2 is 5.06:1. Text tokens otherwise pass: fg/bg is 15.9 and 17.0, and muted is 5.4 or better.

scores.rationale: The most distinctive, and a well-guarded gimmick: a closed ARCADE_COPY vocabulary typed as a TypeScript literal union, font-synthesis: none, and minimum sizes. Even so, Press Start 2P and VT323 are bitmap-style fonts. On the fractional device-pixel ratios common on mid-range Android (2.625, 2.75), the 'multiples of 4px' rule does not give whole device pixels, so pixel glyphs blur. VT323 is unreadable below 20px. Three voices (pixel, VT323, Chakra Petch) mean three type rules for one developer to police on every new screen. Light mode's gold accent cannot be text, and the dark border is too faint to bound anything. HUD totals leak spoilers unless the server filters them, which they note. Blinking, GAME OVER and INSERT COIN will feel tired well before 100 days. Inside the game frame it handles generality reasonably with hit, near and miss tokens and a colour-blind toggle, but the frame's identity does not carry over to calm word or logic games.
scores.contrastProblems: The dark --border #4A4970 is 2.16:1 on the surface, too faint for any edge that has to be seen. The gold #FFC629 is 1.55:1 on the light surface and 1.37:1 on bg. Light bad on surface-2 is 4.65:1, a narrow pass. The 1ST gold rank in light mode (#8A6100) is 5.45:1, which passes.

graftIdeas.idea: Games declare HUD readouts as data, e.g. readouts(view) => [{label:'GUESS', value:'3/7'}], and the platform renders them. New games never style their own status text, and every game's HUD looks the same.

HIT, NEAR and MISS states that differ by luminance, not hue (fg fill, accent fill, surface-2), so they are colour-blind-safe by construction, plus a 'one accent fill per screen' rule that lights only the next action.

Define derived accent tokens such as --color-accent-ink in @theme inline so color-mix() is inlined into each utility and follows per-game --accent overrides. Add registry.test.ts checks for the accent luminance band, for raw Tailwind palette classes under src/games, and for tabular-nums used without font-num.
Fixed-width solid redaction bars for the spoiler wall: the real data is never sent and bar length leaks nothing. Use a clip-path wipe to reveal, never blur.

A src/games/kit.tsx of Cell, Key, LedgerRow and Hatch with written rules for chart, map and quote games, so future games get the house look for free and show state by shape or glyph as well as colour.
Compute hub and overall Today totals on the server using only the games the viewer has finished. This fixes a spoiler leak that exists today.
Leaderboard depth bars whose width is points ÷ leader's points. The bar shows the gap to the leader as real data, and the ▲/▼ delta always pairs the arrow and sign with colour.
An optional backPattern per game (lattice, stripes, dots and so on), hashed from the game id by default, so a seventh game that reuses a palette colour still looks distinct without relying on hue.
Finished game cards stay visibly 'pressed in' at full text contrast. Raised means still to play and settled means done, so you can read the day's state at a glance.

A '👋 Nudge' button that calls navigator.share with a pre-filled poke, so it lands in the real group chat with no push infrastructure. Pair it with a spoiler-safe finishedBy() server query that returns only profile and finished_at.

Enforce a closed copy vocabulary with a TypeScript literal-union type rather than by convention. On a loss, show the countdown to the next puzzle ('come back tomorrow') instead of a red failure state.

Games never call audio or vibrate directly. They emit feedback('key'|'submit'|'solve'|'fail') and the platform applies the user's toggles, so haptics are consistent across games with no per-game code.

judges.bestBlend: Use Broadsheet as the base and add Instrument's machinery. Broadsheet supplies the identity: ink on paper, a rule-based flat layout, Newsreader with Libre Franklin at about 87 KB, the edition and folio ritual, redaction-bar spoilers, and the luminance-band accents with derived tokens inlined through @theme inline. That gives the calm, distinctive and cheap shell. Instrument supplies the engineering contract inside the frame: game-declared readouts drawn by the platform, the luminance-based HIT/NEAR/MISS vocabulary, which fits Broadsheet's ink-plus-one-spot-color rule exactly (HIT is fg ink, NEAR is the game's spot ink, MISS is surface-2, all with glyph or hatch backups), the one-lit-accent 'next up' rule, and the feedback() event API for haptics. Both directions already agree on a flat look, a single small radius, hairline rules, transform- and opacity-only motion, and a luminance band near 0.20–0.25, so they merge without conflicting tokens. Drop Instrument's JetBrains Mono and Inter (Newsreader's tabular figures already handle the numbers) and its dot grid (Broadsheet's light-only grain is enough). Also take Closing Bell's server-side rule that hub totals count only games the viewer has finished, and its proportional depth bars, drawn as hairline spot-ink underlines on the agate table.

recommendation.blendWith: Instrument's play-frame contract (data-declared readouts, luminance-separated HIT/NEAR/MISS, one lit control per screen, a single feedback() API). Read Receipts' social pull redrawn in print style (an 'In today's edition' finisher row, 'finished 8:02' sealed rows, a 'Yesterday's final' strip), without bubbles, typing dots or a realtime dependency. Toy Box's settled Done rows. Closing Bell's spoiler-safe server totals and proportional depth bars, drawn as spot-ink hairlines.
recommendation.why: Broadsheet ranked first with all three judges and scored highest on average (8.56; Instrument was second at 8.00). It is the only direction that is strong on ritual (edition No., headline, bylines, redaction bars), on calm (a black-and-white platform where the only color is each game's single spot ink) and on generality (a luminance-gated ink palette plus a kit that already covers word, grid, number, map, chart and quote games). It is also cheap: two variable fonts at about 87 KB, flat elevation, and motion limited to transform, opacity and clip-path. Instrument is the right engine to put under it. Both already agree on flat surfaces, one small radius, hairline rules and a 0.20–0.25 luminance band, so the two merge with no conflicting tokens. The one real weakness, coldness, is fixed with people (faces, finish times, rivals, yesterday's winner), not with decoration. That warmth lasts 300 days; confetti and candy do not. Changes from the Broadsheet proposal: the orange game ink #CF6B26 is swapped for rose #D45D87 because it sat about 13° from the house vermilion. The house vermilion is kept off every error state. All pairs below were recomputed with a WCAG script.

finalTypography.notes: Newsreader (variable wght only; no opsz axis, no italic; about 58 KB) is used for the nameplate, titles, headlines and every number. Its default digits are already tabular. Libre Franklin (variable, about 29 KB) is used for UI, body, buttons, kickers and inputs. Its Google build has no tnum, so it is never used for numbers. Enforce this with a registry test that fails on any `tabular-nums` used without `font-num`. Load both with next/font/google, latin subset, display:swap, and the default adjustFontFallback (Georgia/Arial metric match). Scale: nameplate 34/1 at 700 and -0.02em; page and game title 32/1.1 at 600; greeting and headline 22–24/1.2; index-row game name 20/1.2; body 15/1.45; inputs 16px; kicker Franklin 700, 11px, uppercase, 0.08em, muted (never font-variant small-caps). The result score is clamp(56px,18cqi,80px)/0.9; agate points 20px at 600; folio countdown 13px at 500. 11px is the floor and only for 700-weight uppercase kickers. No italics, no blackletter, no serif on buttons. Drop Instrument's Inter and JetBrains Mono; Newsreader already does their job.

finalShape.texture: Newsprint grain in light mode only: body { background-image: url(/grain.png); background-size: 128px 128px } (a 128×128 grayscale noise PNG, black at alpha 0–10/255, about 4 KB, scrolling and not fixed). Dark mode is background-image:none. Never on surfaces or inside .puzzle-frame, which always paints solid bg-surface. Hatch pattern for NEAR, eliminated and wrong states: repeating-linear-gradient(45deg, color-mix(in oklab, var(--fg) 25%, transparent) 0 1px, transparent 1px 5px).
finalShape.notes: Structure comes from rules, not boxes. Three weights: hairline 1px var(--border), which is decorative at 1.41–1.5:1 and only divides rows; heavy 2px var(--fg) above section headers and under table headers; masthead thick-thin (3px fg, 2px gap, 1px fg) used only under the nameplate and above the Final box. A single radius --radius-card of 4px for cards, buttons, inputs, spot blocks and tiles. Kit cells use 2px and redaction bars 1px. The only circles are avatars. Anything whose edge carries meaning gets an fg border for WCAG 1.4.11: underline inputs (border-b 1.5px fg), secondary buttons (1.5px fg outline), and the puzzle frame (1px fg). Focus is 2px solid fg with a 2px offset (13.9:1 or better everywhere). Tap targets: buttons h-12, index rows at least 76px, agate rows at least 56px, tabs and segments h-11. Derived colors MUST be declared in @theme inline so they resolve per element under game --accent overrides: --color-accent-ink: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 66%, var(--fg)) (verified at least 5.01:1 on every light surface and at least 5.98:1 on every dark surface for all 7 inks); --color-highlight: color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent) 14%, var(--surface)) (fg 14.1:1 or better and muted 5.74:1 or better in light; fg 11.85:1 and muted 5.44:1 or better in dark); --color-on-accent: #14120E (4.85–5.29:1 on game inks, 4.72:1 on house vermilion). Verified base pairs: fg/bg 15.32 (light) and 15.06 (dark); muted is at least 5.64 on every surface; good and bad are at least 5.16 (light) and 5.60 (dark) on surface-2, and about 5.0 on their own 14% tints. Game inks as graphics measure 3.09 or better on light bg and 4.0 or better on dark surfaces, but only 2.78–3.05 on light surface-2. The kit therefore always outlines cells in fg and adds a hatch or glyph, so no state depends on the ink edge. Avatars are oklch(0.89 0.045 h) in light and oklch(0.34 0.045 h) in dark, with an fg Newsreader initial (worst case 12.37:1 light and 9.28:1 dark).

signatureMoments.design: The nameplate (the group's paper name, Newsreader 700 34px, centered) sits over the thick-thin rule. The folio line in Franklin 11px/600 caps reads 'MON, OCT 5 · No. 214 · NEXT 06:12:45'; the numerals are font-num and the countdown is shown in the user's local time. Under the folio is a 2px day-progress hairline in house vermilion, filled to the fraction of the New York day that has passed (from Instrument). Then 'Good morning, Ashwin.' and a fixed-template factual headline of 48 characters or fewer, built only from spoiler-safe data ('Priya leads the week by 14.' / 'Fresh edition. Nobody's on the board yet.'). Below that is the 'In today's edition' row: monogram avatars of friends who have finished something, each with a row of 4px squares under it, one per live game, filled with that game's ink once that friend has finished it (status only, never scores). It is cheap static markup, not conic rings or realtime.

The platform owns the order. (1) The game finishes its own last reveal and calls revealDone(); the host forces this at 2s. (2) A 300ms hold on the final board. (3) The Final box mounts below the frame: the thick-thin rule draws in with scaleX over 280ms, then the kicker 'FINAL · SOLVED IN 4', then the score in Newsreader, faded in and risen 6px over 220ms (no count-up), with 'pts' in Franklin muted, then a deck line ('2nd of 5 so far today.'). (4) Share gets focus. (5) Only then does the spoiler wall unseal. A loss uses the identical layout with an fg numeral, the kicker 'FINAL · THE NUMBER WAS 61', and a line 'Next edition in 6h 12m' (Coin-Op's CONTINUE? without the costume). Tapping skips to the end state. Reduced motion collapses everything to a 120ms crossfade in the same order.

The exact paste text sits in a clipping: a 1px dashed muted border with a 12px ✂ glyph on the top-left edge, Franklin 15px pre-line, the emoji grid at 22px, byte-for-byte what will be sent. Line 1 is '🔢 Number Hunt · No. 214 · Oct 5', then the native label and points, then the grid (at most 8 columns × 6 rows, allowlisted single-codepoint emoji), then a deep link to /play/number-hunt. The button is full-width h-12, the screen's one lit control (bg-accent, on-accent ink), labelled 'Share to the group'. It uses the native share sheet on touch devices; on the clipboard path the label reads 'Copied, paste it in the chat ✓' for 2s and the clipping border flashes solid 1.5px accent for 600ms. When every live game is done, the hub offers 'Share my day': one message with the date, the edition No., the day total, one line per game and a single link.

Below the frame, before you finish: a heavy rule, then the kicker 'FRIENDS' RESULTS · SEALED 🔒', then one row per friend who has finished, showing avatar, name and 'finished 8:02' in muted. Their label and score cells are fixed-width solid fg redaction bars (h-3.5 w-24 and h-3.5 w-10, rounded-[1px]), so bar length leaks nothing. Friends with an in_progress play show 'playing' in muted. Caption: 'Finish today's puzzle to unseal.' The server never sends hidden data (a finishedBy() query returns only profile and finished_at), and blur is never used. Skeletons are surface-2 blocks with no label, so the two cannot be confused. After the Final sequence, the bars wipe left to right (clip-path inset over 320ms, 40ms stagger) into the font-num values, and your own row slots into score order. The same bars fill PTS and native-label cells on any per-game board that includes today for a game you haven't finished.

At 00:00 New York time the day-progress hairline completes and resets, the edition numeral slides from 214 to 215 (out and up, in from below, 260ms), and router.refresh() runs after 400ms. Index rows reset to Play and the folio right reads 'TODAY'S EDITION IS OUT'. If the PWA was backgrounded across midnight, a visibilitychange date check shows a slim h-11 bg-fg/text-bg banner, 'New edition · No. 215. Tap to refresh'. Mid-play, the frame keeps yesterday's puzzle and the sticky bar says 'No. 214 · yesterday's edition'. If a move returns day_over, the board is replaced by a calm card ('Yesterday's puzzle closed while you were playing. Today's is ready.'). On the first open of a new day, a dismissible 'Yesterday's final' strip leads the hub: the overall winner, your place and the closest finish. The day is stamped 'Final' early once every active player (anyone who played in the last 7 days) has finished.

Agate rows carry a stock-table change mark under the name: '▲2' in good or '▼1' in bad, font-num 12px. The glyph carries the meaning, so color is never the only cue, and ties render 'T-2'. Deltas are measured against the last-seen standings for that board and period (sessionStorage, try/catch) and against the previous day on the server for Week/All-time. When you return to a board after finishing, rows reorder with a FLIP translateY over 240ms, your highlight row steps from 20% to 14% accent over 600ms, and the headline updates ('You move to 2nd this week.'). A rival line sits under the hub standings: '12 behind Sam for 2nd this week' (or 'Priya is 8 behind you'). It only ever compares you with the one person next to you.

A finished game's index row recedes: bg-surface-2, no button, and on the right a 28px Newsreader score with the kicker 'PTS ✓' in good. All text stays at full contrast and nothing is dimmed. The next unfinished game's Play button is the only lit (spot-ink filled) control on the hub; other unplayed rows get a 1.5px fg outline Play. With unplayed games sorted first, today's status reads at a glance. When all are done, the index header changes to 'ALL IN · No. 214' and the Share my day action appears.

The streak sits in the folio as 'RUN 12' with Newsreader numerals, plus a 7-cell tick strip on Profile (filled fg = played, outlined = missed, ❄ = frozen). There is no 🔥 in the chrome; it stays in the share text. Any one finished game keeps the run alive. After 8pm local, if nothing is finished, the folio run reads 'RUN 12 · PLAY ONE TO KEEP IT' in muted: no red, no modal, no exclamation. At 7/30/100/365 days, or on taking the group's longest current run, a one-time 'NOTICE' box appears (2px fg top rule, Newsreader 18px line), dismissed by tap.

Testing games show a 'PROOF' kicker in a 1px dashed muted box on their index row and play header, and Admin is 'The Desk'. Every game header carries 'Set by Ashwin' (optional setBy field). When a game goes live, the hub shows a one-day Notice ('New in the paper: Chart Guess, set by Ashwin') with a one-line designer note. For its first 7 days the game is in preseason: it has its own board but does not count toward Overall.

aggregateRanking.verdict: Primary. All three judges ranked it first: the most coherent ritual, a calm black-and-white platform where each game is one spot ink, a luminance-gated palette that works in both themes, and a kit that covers every planned genre. Watch that it doesn't feel stuffy; warmth comes from people, not decoration.

Blend in as the engine, not the brand. Take its readouts-as-data HUD, luminance-separated HIT/NEAR/MISS, one-lit-control rule and feedback() API. Reject its monochrome avatars, Inter/JetBrains stack, dot grid and a game accent that duplicates the house accent. On its own it reads as a Linear clone.
Graft only 'Done stays pressed in' (as settled surface-2 rows). Its 2px ink outlines, lips and candy fills are a 2021-era trend that gets noisy on dense boards and has a weaker dark mode.

Graft its data honesty: server-side spoiler-safe totals, proportional depth-to-leader bars, and arrow-plus-sign deltas. Reject the terminal skin; it is Ashwin's identity, not the group's, it uses pale fills that vanish in light mode, and it puts a ticker in motion on a calm hub.

Graft the 'what the group sees' share preview and an optional hashed per-game pattern for telling games apart past 6. Reject the skeuomorphism: linen, felt, lamp and lattice wear thin, cost about 200–250 KB of fonts, and the light accent fails 3:1 on bg.

The best social instincts; graft them in print grammar (who finished and when, an 'In today's edition' row, yesterday's winner). Reject the chat skin and the Phase-2 realtime dependency. It imitates the group chat it sits beside and gets busy fast.

Reject. A pixel-font costume with poor longevity and legibility (VT323 needs 20px or more, bitmap fonts blur at fractional DPR), and the dark border at 2.16:1 fails the pressable cue. Keep only the idea that a loss leads into a countdown to tomorrow.

graftedIdeas: Instrument: games declare HUD readouts as data (readouts(view) => [{label:'GUESS', value:'3/7'}]); the platform renders them as kicker-over-Newsreader cells divided by hairlines above the frame. Games never style their own status text.

Instrument and Broadsheet: HIT/NEAR/MISS/EMPTY state vocabulary separated by luminance and shape, not hue. HIT = fg ink fill with a bg glyph (13.9:1 or better against MISS); NEAR = the game's spot ink with the 45° hatch and a 14120E glyph; MISS = surface-2 with a muted glyph; EMPTY = surface with fg cell lines. Correct and wrong verdicts also carry ✓ or ✕. Colour-blind safe by construction and consistent with the ink-plus-one-spot rule.
Instrument: one lit control per screen. The spot-ink fill moves from the next-up Play to Start to Share; everything else is fg-outlined or ink-filled.

Instrument and Toy Box: games never call navigator.vibrate or audio directly. They call fx.invalid/accepted/hit/solved/failed/select/announce and the platform maps each call to motion, haptics, aria-live and (later) sound, respecting the user's toggles.
Broadsheet: fixed-width solid redaction bars for sealed results, never blur, with hidden data never sent. Revealed with a clip-path wipe after your own Final.
Broadsheet: edition number (days since EDITION_EPOCH) in the folio, sticky bar and share text, plus fixed-template factual headlines built only from data already on screen.
Broadsheet: 'Set by Ashwin' bylines, 'PROOF' labels for testing games, and 'The Desk' for admin, so the owner-as-setter is part of the product.
Broadsheet: a registry.test.ts gate requiring accent relative luminance in [0.22, 0.25], no raw Tailwind palette classes under src/games, and no tabular-nums without font-num.
Read Receipts: sealed rows show who finished and when ('finished 8:02') and who is playing, never the outcome; served by a spoiler-safe finishedBy()/dayProgress() query.
Read Receipts, in print grammar: an 'In today's edition' row of finisher avatars with per-game spot-ink progress squares (static, no realtime, no conic rings).
Closing Bell: every board that includes today counts only the games the viewer has finished (server-side); other friends' pending games show as a spot-ink dot with a footnote.
Closing Bell: a depth-to-leader bar as a 2px spot-ink hairline under each agate row, with width = points ÷ leader's points.
Closing Bell and the UX brainstorm: a dismissible 'Yesterday's final' strip on the first open of each day, and the day stamped 'Final' early once all active players have finished.
Toy Box: finished rows settle onto surface-2 at full contrast and unplayed rows sort first, so what's left today reads at a glance.
Card Table: a 'what the group sees' literal share preview (the clipping) and an optional backPattern per game, hashed from the id, for telling games apart once ink colours repeat past 6.
Coin-Op: a loss ends with a countdown to the next edition rather than a red failure state.

crossCuttingUx.area: Spoiler wall: close the side doors
crossCuttingUx.decision: One server function, getVisibleStandings(viewerId, scope, period, date), is the only way any board that includes today is built (hub, leaderboard, headline, rival line, Share my day). For each friend it hides today's points for games the viewer hasn't finished and returns them as 'pending'. The current hub and the Today leaderboard leak results today, so fix this before any visual work ships.

The platform stages the finish: the game's final reveal (revealDone, forced at 2s), a 300ms hold, the Final box, Share focused, and only then the spoiler unseal. The current same-paint refresh() that swaps LockedResults for friends' results is replaced by a client-side SpoilerGate.

On /play/*, hide the bottom nav and the app header. Use a 48px sticky bar (← Today, emoji and name, No. 214), the readouts strip, a message slot overlaying the top edge of the board (no layout shift), the frame sized with container queries so it never scrolls, and a controls dock padded by env(safe-area-inset-bottom). Set touch-action:manipulation and overscroll-behavior:contain.

A platform GameKeyboard (qwerty, numeric or custom keys; 56px keys; gutters inside the hit area; pointerdown for symbols, click for Enter; Backspace repeats while held; per-key state) plus useGameKeys for desktop keyboards. Discrete-symbol games never use native inputs. Migrate Number Hunt off <input type=number autoFocus>.

On submit, lock the row with a 90ms press immediately. Public-rule validation (range, duplicates, word list) runs on the client so an invalid move shakes at once; the server still re-validates. Show a spinner only after 600ms. Buffer keystrokes during a reveal. Never dim the board while a move is pending.

dayState drives the hub layout: fresh, in_progress, done, final. Unplayed games sort first and done rows settle. The 'done' state shows the day total, the provisional rank and Share my day, and makes the next-edition countdown prominent.

Default period is This week (Mon–Sun New York time), and the hub's mini standings are weekly too. All-time becomes a stats table (average, weeks won, best run) rather than cumulative points, which only reward seniority. Players who haven't played are collapsed into one muted line on the boards and are never ranked as zero rows.
One line under the hub standings comparing you only with the adjacent person on the weekly board, computed from spoiler-safe data.

Share text includes the edition No. and deep-links to /play/<gameId>. A combined 'Share my day' message is offered when all games are done. Registry tests enforce share grids of at most 8 columns × 6 rows using allowlisted single-codepoint emoji. The clipping preview is byte-for-byte what gets pasted.
Any one finished game keeps the run. After 8pm local with nothing finished, a quiet muted folio line appears. No red, no modal, no all-games requirement.

A /join/<code> link prefills the invite code and shows an avatar stack of members ('Join Ashwin, Priya + 4'). After signup the user goes straight to Today, with a '👋 Rohan joined' notice for existing members. An Add-to-Home-Screen sheet appears after the first finished game.
Every empty state names a person or an action ('You could be first today', 'You're first. Results fill in as friends finish', 'Your history starts today').

State is always shown by shape or glyph as well as colour. Accent text only through accent-ink. Focus is a 2px fg outline. One polite aria-live region fed by fx.announce. Board semantics (role=grid, cell labels, arrow keys) are part of the game contract before the third game ships.

Honour prefers-reduced-motion and an in-app 'Reduce motion' toggle (html[data-motion=reduce], per device). Every transform and clip-path animation becomes a 120ms opacity crossfade, FLIP is skipped, and the information order stays the same.

Committed moves sync through the existing version/stale mechanism. Unscored scratch state (half-typed input, pencil marks) lives per device in localStorage under user:game:date. On focus or visibilitychange, re-fetch and show 'Picked up from your other device'. No leave-page confirms.

Android-only, feature-detected, fired only through fx: select 8ms, hit 12ms, reject [20,60,20], solved [15,70,15,70,40], failed 90ms. The toggle is hidden on iOS. No per-keypress buzz and no iOS switch hack.
Earned automatically: one ❄ per 7 straight days, bank up to 2, applied to a single missed day without any action. Computed in streaks() SQL with no stock table and nothing to buy.
A Monday recap Notice that can be shared as text. A 👑 next to the champion's avatar for the week. 3–4 data-derived awards, at most one per person. A 'full house' day count that only ever goes up.
A 'You vs Sam' record on profiles: overall and per game, only on days you both played, with a last-10 strip. No challenge mechanics.
A launch Notice with the designer note, 7 days of preseason excluded from Overall, and a one-tap difficulty vote after the result that feeds The Desk for tuning the 0–100 scoring.

/admin/sandbox/[gameId] renders fixtures at 360×640 and 390×844, with toggles for theme, high contrast and reduced motion, an 800ms latency switch and a replay-finish button. Passing its checklist is how a game moves from PROOF to live.

Offer only after the app is installed and the person has played on 3 days. At most one notification per person per day: a streak reminder at a chosen time if nothing is played, and an optional 'Day's final'. Never at rollover and never per friend finish.
A fixed set of 5 emoji on unsealed friend rows, visible and usable only by people who finished that game (enforced on the server). No text comments.
Off by default. If built, synthesised in WebAudio from fx events, with audioSession 'ambient'. No audio files.
Past puzzles playable only from Profile, marked 🕰, never on any board and never shareable.

No solve time in the 0–100 score by default and no ticking clock in untimed games. Never build pausable timers or 'active time' heartbeats. A game that truly needs speed declares timing:'scored' and gets an honest, disclosed wall clock.
No repeated daily reminders, red badges, 'your streak will die' copy, hub lists of who hasn't played, or group streaks one person can break. Losses never get harsher styling than wins.
No confetti, particles, count-ups, springs, full-screen win takeovers or shimmer skeletons. The reward is the friends' unseal.
No in-app chat, comment threads, activity feed, XP, levels or badge piles. The group chat is the social space; invest in the share message and the morning recap instead.
No grain, texture, gradients, shadows, motion or platform colour inside .puzzle-frame, and no marquee or ambient animation anywhere. The frame's only colour budget is one spot ink plus good and bad.

platformPrimitives: Tokens in src/app/globals.css: bg/surface/surface-2/border/fg/muted/accent/good/bad (values above) plus --on-accent #14120E. In @theme inline: --color-accent-ink (color-mix oklab 66% accent → fg), --color-highlight (14% accent over surface), --color-on-accent, --font-sans: var(--font-ui), --font-serif and --font-num: var(--font-serif), --radius-card: 0.25rem. Declaring them in @theme inline is required so per-game --accent overrides re-resolve per element.

State tokens for every game: --state-hit (fg fill, bg glyph), --state-near (accent fill + hatch, on-accent glyph), --state-miss (surface-2, muted glyph), --state-empty (surface with fg cell lines); verdicts always carry ✓/✕ glyphs in good/bad.
Utilities: kicker, rule-heavy, rule-masthead, redact, hatch, num (font-num tabular-nums lining-nums).

Motion tokens: --dur-press 80ms, --dur-fast 160ms, --dur-base 220ms, --dur-reveal 320ms, --dur-flip 280ms, --stagger 40ms, --dur-shake 320ms; --ease-out cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1), --ease-in cubic-bezier(.4,0,1,1). Only transform, opacity and clip-path animate; any single move's sequence is 1.2s or less; everything collapses under prefers-reduced-motion or html[data-motion=reduce].

<GameScreen> focus shell for /play/*: 48px sticky bar, a Readouts strip rendered from game-declared data, a MessageSlot overlay, .puzzle-frame (rounded-card border-fg bg-surface p-4, container-type inline-size, games size themselves in cqi), a controls dock with safe-area padding, and the Final box, clipping and SpoilerGate below.

GameDefinition fields: accent (luminance in [0.22,0.25], test-enforced), emoji, section kicker (WORD/LOGIC/NUMBER/MAP/CHART/QUOTE), setBy, designerNote, readouts(view), timing:'untimed'|'scored', controlsHeight, publicValidate(move,puzzle), resultTags(state), preseasonUntil, optional backPattern.
GameUiProps additions: fx.{invalid,accepted,select,hit,solved,failed,announce}, revealDone(), scratch.{get,set,clear} (per device, unscored), prefs.{reducedMotion,highContrast,haptics} (read-only).

src/games/kit.tsx: Cell (crossword square, 1.5px fg lines, state prop), Tile, Key and GameKeyboard (qwerty, numeric or custom; 56px keys), LedgerRow (ruled guess history, font-num 22px), Hatch, Readout, usePointerDrag (8px slop, setPointerCapture, mandatory tap-tap fallback, touch-action:none only on draggables), useGameKeys.

Genre rules in the kit: charts use hairline gridlines, 1.5px fg axes, one accent series and others fg/45 dashed, with font-num axis numerals; maps use surface-2 land, 0.75px fg borders, accent for the selection and hatch for eliminated regions; quotes use Newsreader 22/1.4 with a hanging accent-ink quotation mark.

Server: getVisibleStandings(viewerId, scope, period, date), the only path for any board that includes today; dayProgress(date) giving per-user per-game status with no scores; finishedBy(gameId,date) returning profile and finished_at only; activePlayers(date, 7) for the Final stamp, the full-house count and empty states; editionNumber(date) from EDITION_EPOCH.
Share: shareGameText() with edition No. and a /play/<gameId> deep link; shareDayText() for Share my day; grid of at most 8×6 from the emoji allowlist.

Components: Masthead/Folio, IndexRow, AgateTable (deltas, T-ties, depth hairline, highlight row, redaction cells), FinalBox, Clipping, SpoilerGate/SealedRows, EditionRow (finisher avatars with progress squares), YesterdayFinal, RivalLine, Notice, TickStrip, Avatar (oklch low-chroma monogram).

registry.test.ts conformance: accent luminance band; on-accent at least 4.5:1; no raw Tailwind palette classes or text-accent under src/games; no tabular-nums without font-num; share-grid size and allowlist; rules of 4 bullets or fewer.
/admin/sandbox/[gameId] (The Desk): fixtures, two phone frames, theme, contrast and motion toggles, latency switch, replay finish; the PROOF → live checklist.
openQuestionsForOwner: What is the paper called? The nameplate becomes the app's identity. It should be the group's own name, not 'The Daily' (an NYT podcast name).
HIT colour: commit to solid ink for 'correct' (calm, colour-blind safe, on-brand), or keep Wordle-style green for correct at the cost of the one-spot-ink rule?
Is the serif-and-rules newspaper voice right for your friends? Test the hub with 2–3 of them in week one before polishing the rest.
Weekly race scoring: plain sum of 7 days, or best 6 of 7 so one missed day doesn't knock someone out?
Nudges: allow a '👋 Nudge' that opens the share sheet with a poke for one friend, or forbid naming non-players anywhere (the recommendation is to forbid it for v1)?

The [0.22, 0.25] luminance band rules out bright yellows, limes and pastels for future games (yellow becomes ochre). Accept that constraint for one-hex-both-themes, or allow per-theme accent pairs with more test burden?
Should any of your future games ever score speed (timing:'scored'), or is the paper strictly untimed?
EDITION_EPOCH: does No. 1 start on the group's first real day, or a symbolic date?
Light-mode newsprint grain: keep the subtle texture, or go perfectly flat paper?
Reactions on unsealed results: worth building later, or does all banter belong in the real group chat?
